scores.rationale: Across the four calls there is no buyback or dividend policy discussed; instead the FY26 capital action is a dilutive preferential warrant issue to the promoter to fund acquisitions.
scores.quote: our corporate promoter, Affle Holdings, will invest to acquire ~7.4 million warrants at INR 1,487, totaling approximately INR 11 billion

scores.rationale: The business is genuinely asset-light with strong cash conversion (OCF INR 5.02bn in FY26, OCF/PAT target >80% and historically 90-100%), and the protecting moat is real but IP/integration-based rather than structural.
scores.quote: We achieved operating cash flows of INR 5.02 billion during the year, increasing by ~25% CAGR over the last 5 years

scores.rationale: Affle has consistently grown faster than the digital ad industry average with a small absolute share of a large market, though growth has decelerated from 128% y-o-y in FY23 to ~19-20% now.
scores.quote: having achieved about 45% organic growth (which was well above the industry average growth trend)

scores.rationale: Multi-year, well-executed expansion across India, global emerging markets and developed markets (26-28% of revenue growing 18%), backed by a dedicated North America CEO hire and vertical launches across international markets.
scores.quote: We have successfully onboarded Sameer Sondhi as our CEO for North America with a dual role as our Chief Strategic Investments Officer

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume-led — conversions rose from 61.9m to 120.3m while the CPCU rate crept from Rs.52 to Rs.60 over four years (+3.1% y-o-y in Q3 FY26) — and gross margin has compressed as inventory/data cost rose to 63.3%.
scores.quote: It is guided by driving higher volumes of conversions

scores.rationale: Ad-spend cyclicality is acknowledged (developed-market pullback for 1.5 years then normalization, geopolitical softness in Q4 FY26), but there is no evidence the company is positioned at a cycle bottom with an identifiable upturn ahead.
scores.quote: temporary softness in select markets and verticals during the quarter due to the geopolitical events

scores.rationale: The end market is in secular expansion — under-penetrated digital share of ad spend in emerging markets plus AI-driven expansion of ROI-based advertising — a theme management has articulated consistently since 2022 and delivered against.
scores.quote: the shift that I'm talking about from traditional spends to more digital spends in emerging markets is a mega trend

scores.rationale: Predominantly organic growth with prudent working capital, a debt-light balance sheet and stated capital-allocation discipline, tempered by an active multi-target acquisition search funded by an INR 11bn promoter warrant issue.
scores.quote: We remain disciplined in capital allocation while ensuring that we continue to invest and innovate proactively to strengthen our long-term moat

scores.rationale: Founder-led management has articulated and delivered a consistent multi-year plan (Affle2.0 to Affle 3i 10x vision) meeting its 20% CAGR medium-term guidance across five years and 13 consecutive quarters of sequential topline growth.
scores.quote: for the last 5 years, we have delivered on our medium-term guidance across both top line and profitability

scores.rationale: Commentary is markedly promotional — long recitations of awards, rankings and market-cap creation, plus superlative self-description — rather than substance-over-celebrity understatement.
scores.quote: we are clearly a thought leader like none other in the Adtech ecosystem in India

scores.rationale: There is evidence of a built-out leadership layer (20 CXOs/VPs globally), an internal promotion to COO, and systematic AI upskilling of teams, though senior bench-building is partly via external hires.
scores.quote: we had internally promoted Vipul Kedia, as our Chief Operating Officer to anchor our growth in India and emerging markets

scores.rationale: Management pre-guides and then explains variances (higher effective tax rate flagged two quarters ahead, RMG provision, OCF/PAT dip to 75.8% with a stated cause and normalization timeline), but tends to reframe negatives such as gross-margin compression as 'investment' rather than owning them plainly.
scores.quote: Our OCF to PAT for the nine months stood at 75.8%. This is because of a temporary increase in collection days from Agencies

scores.rationale: Strong reported results sit alongside signals that complicate a pure skill read — decelerating growth, steadily rising inventory/data cost, and heavy self-promotion — so the assessment is only partly robust to the halo effect.
scores.quote: we are continuously seeing a reduction in the margins from a percentage perspective

scores.rationale: The CPCU outcome-based model plus deep first-party data integration creates a distinctive position in advertisers' minds that management argues rivals cannot easily match, but this falls short of monopoly-like standing in a crowded adtech market.
scores.quote: a lot of them are not on the CPCU business model and a lot of them are also not directly deeply integrated with the advertisers' first-party data

scores.rationale: Switching costs arise from conversion-level first-party data integrations and vertical-specific intelligence built per advertiser, creating lock-in without a true regional or aftermarket monopoly.
scores.quote: integrating as part of our unique CPCU business model with deeper conversion level, first-party data integrations with our advertisers directly

scores.rationale: The industry is not a stable oligopoly — walled gardens dominate and agencies/advertisers retain negotiating power, evidenced by agency payment-cycle pressure and repeated analyst questions about competitive pricing.
scores.quote: In terms of the walled gardens, on AI side, the automation tools that the walled gardens are providing, I believe that's definitely helping them

scores.rationale: Patents and verticalized data provide some barrier and management insists it does not compete on price, yet gross margins have compressed for 7-8 straight quarters and adtech remains structurally easy to enter.
scores.quote: we are not fighting the competition on pricing. We are fighting them on value

scores.rationale: Management identifies weaker rivals specifically unable to serve premium iOS and CTV inventory in emerging markets, from whom Affle is taking premium wallet share.
scores.quote: most of the competitors in emerging markets at least, are not very strong on the iOS platforms

scores.rationale: Affle is a widely covered listed company with 385,000+ shareholders, multiple broker-hosted calls and constant award publicity — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: we celebrate Affle's 3rd IPO anniversary together with our 385,000+ shareholders

scores.rationale: Pricing is outcome-linked rather than image-driven and gross margin has steadily eroded (inventory and data cost rising to 63.3% of revenue from ~50-58% historically), indicating limited intangible pricing power.
scores.quote: our inventory and data costs stood at 63.3% of the revenues for the quarter, an increase of approximately 90 basis points sequentially

scores.rationale: Customers buy measurable certainty — pay-per-conversion ROI, privacy compliance (DPTM certification) and patented human-versus-non-human fraud filtration — making trust central, though price still features in advertiser negotiations.
scores.quote: strengthening our position as a privacy-compliant, trusted and results-driven platform

scores.rationale: A consistently high direct-advertiser mix (70-75%) with a sales organization driven on explicit growth KPIs indicates genuine customer intimacy and access.
scores.quote: direct versus agency, it's within that range, 70% to 75% direct business

scores.rationale: The customer base is corporate/enterprise and the value proposition is correctly matched to it — measurable ROI/TCO plus data-integration switching costs rather than consumer-style intangibles.
scores.quote: we have a large part of our business anchored on enterprise customers who are not going anywhere anytime soon

scores.rationale: A deep, multi-product technology stack (Newton, Niko agentic AI, OpticksAI) backed by ~300 enforceable patent claims spanning fraud intelligence and human-versus-non-human distillation delivers a demonstrably superior customer benefit.
scores.quote: our patents span across fraud intelligence, human versus nonhuman distillation, precision targeting, contextual and gesture-based advertising

scores.rationale: There is a data-scale feedback loop from conversions feeding targeting intelligence, but management never describes a self-reinforcing two-sided network and the flywheel is not evidenced in the excerpts.

Deep OEM, app-store, operator and CTV partnerships (TCL, Oppo, Honor) give access to premium inventory across markets that management argues competitors cannot replicate, though this is inventory reach rather than an unmatched service network.
scores.quote: TCL... is one of the largest CTV Android makers in the world, globally... therefore, these kind of partnerships are important

scores.rationale: Capex is overwhelmingly greenfield growth capex — Rs.275cr of Rs.310cr in FY26 and Rs.380-400cr guided for FY27 for 60 new facilities — against a low-capex model where a secondary centre costing Rs.4.5-7cr reaches 32-33% store margins by year five, and EBITDA margins still expanded while expanding.
scores.quote: Since FY '23, we have added 148 new greenfield facilities in total, a 5.7x growth in annual greenfield additions from just 10 facilities four years ago.

scores.rationale: Marketing spend is modest and lightly disclosed (a one-time Rs.4cr production cost) but management repeatedly attributes faster new-centre ramp-ups and 25% walk-in growth to brand equity, suggesting A&P is compounding rather than rented.
scores.quote: The ramp-up across recently launched facilities has been faster than earlier phases, supported by strengthening brand equity

scores.rationale: R&D is clinical/academic (340 to 360 international publications over three decades) plus an in-house hospital management system, which supports capability and credibility but is not a product-revenue engine with measurable R&D efficiency.
scores.quote: We have a new software called Neo, which is a next-generation AI-ready hospital management system developed by our in-house technology team

scores.rationale: Past bolt-ons in Punjab, Maharashtra and Gujarat were small and complementary with deferred consideration winding down, but the AEHL related-party merger drew repeated, unanswered minority objections on the swap ratio, offsetting the good record.
scores.quote: the merger ratio just seems very off. It is 30% lower than what any basic analysis would suggest

scores.rationale: No dividend, buyback or distribution policy is discussed in any of the excerpts; capital returned to the balance sheet via Rs.195cr of IPO-funded debt repayment is deleveraging, not distribution.

The model is explicitly asset-light — 220 of 221 facilities leased, Rs.30-35 lakh capex for a primary centre and Rs.10-12cr for a tertiary generating Rs.15-16cr revenue by year five — combined with a brand and clinical-talent moat.
scores.quote: We work on an asset-light model, enabling us to scale effectively with minimum capex.

scores.rationale: India's eye care market is dominated by standalone practitioners, so despite being the largest chain the company has long runway, and it is visibly capturing share via 52-55 facility additions a year and 25% growth in daily walk-ins.
scores.quote: Every day, nearly 10,000 patients now walk into our facilities across our network, up from about 8,000 patients in the previous financial year.

scores.rationale: Expansion from a southern base into Maharashtra, Gujarat, Delhi NCR, Rajasthan, Odisha and Africa has been executed to plan, with the Delhi anchor centre profitable from month one and North guided to its highest-ever 16 additions.
scores.quote: This facility has emerged as the anchor of our Delhi NCR cluster, delivering strong performance from the very first month of operations.

scores.rationale: Growth is roughly half value, half volume, with value driven by mix (high-end cataract from 22.5% to 26.3%, Femto up 87%) rather than price, since headline price hikes run only 2-3% a year.
scores.quote: supported by near equal contributions from both volume and value of close to 14%

scores.rationale: Eye care is largely non-cyclical; the only cycle referenced is a soft refractive year attributed to the industry with an expected rebound, too small a segment (~5%) to constitute cycle-bottom positioning.
scores.quote: It is more to do with the overall industry being slightly slow on the refractive side this year.

scores.rationale: Demand is in permanent secular expansion — an ageing population, under-penetrated eye care in Tier 2/3 India, and rising adoption of higher-end procedures — evidenced by 30 lakh patients and 3.23 lakh surgeries in FY26 with consistent ~20%+ growth.
scores.quote: expanding significantly into high-potential underserved markets through strategic facility opening

scores.rationale: The trajectory is organic greenfield expansion with no large M&A, systematic deleveraging of Rs.195cr from IPO proceeds, funded from internal cash (CFO/EBITDA ~84%), and margins protected through the heaviest expansion year.
scores.quote: So we predominantly are focusing only on organic expansion.

scores.rationale: Across seven calls the team set and then met multi-year commitments — the 45-50 annual facility target, the 3-year merger promise pursued through SEBI and NCLT, and a 5.7x scaling of the greenfield engine over four years.
scores.quote: We set out this year with clear guidance on growth, profitability and expansion, and we delivered on each one.

scores.rationale: The family-run group listed only in February 2025 after decades of low-profile operation and the calls are dense with unit economics rather than promotion, though listing and broad sell-side coverage have raised the profile.
scores.quote: I would like to welcome you all to Dr. Agarwal's Health Care's maiden earnings call as a publicly listed entity.

scores.rationale: Talent development is systematic and scaled — crossing 1,000 doctors, ~140 doctors in advanced training during FY26, and a deepened internal leadership bench with a CBO, COO and CSO appearing on later calls.
scores.quote: for the first time in our history, we have a total doctor strength of over 1,000 doctors across our network

scores.rationale: Disclosure quality is unusually high — format-wise capex, maturity curves, store-level margins, an explicit IndAS-to-iGAAP bridge, and capex actual vs commitment — but on the merger ratio management deflected to fairness opinions rather than engaging the substance of minority objections.
scores.quote: you just have to subtract 7% to 7.5% from the Ind AS margin to derive the actual iGAAP margins

scores.rationale: Headline growth is flattered by IPO/PE-funded centre additions and deleveraging, but skill is separable in the underlying data — 14% same-store growth on pre-FY22 facilities and margins held at ~28.5% through 52 openings.
scores.quote: those which were opened prior to FY '22, contributed INR1,375 crores in revenue, reflecting a strong 14% same-store sales growth

scores.rationale: The brand approaches top-of-mind status for eye care in its core southern markets, driving footfall directly rather than through referral, though this is a mind-share position rather than a structural monopoly.
scores.quote: the strength of our brand recall and our ability to deliver quality eye care close to where patients live

scores.rationale: Cluster density gives regional leadership in Tamil Nadu and Telangana, but eye surgery is largely episodic and elective so genuine switching costs or captive aftermarket lock-in are weak.
scores.quote: We remain focused on sustaining our market leadership in both Tamil Nadu and Telangana

scores.rationale: The Indian eye care market is fragmented among standalone practitioners rather than a stable oligopoly, though the individual retail patient has no negotiating power given 62-72% cash payment.
scores.quote: Our payer mix for YTD December 2025 stood at 62.4% from cash

scores.rationale: Pricing behaviour is rational with no discount war and steady 2-3% annual increases, and clinical talent plus cluster build-out is a real barrier, but the modest price increase also signals limited pricing latitude against low-cost local competition.
scores.quote: In the last two, three years, we've seen an average price increase of about 2% to 3% per year.

scores.rationale: The expansion thesis is built on entering underserved Tier 2/3 micro-markets served by weaker standalone clinics, which management targets systematically, though competitor weakness is implied rather than explicitly evidenced.
scores.quote: we aim to deepen our presence in the underserved regions of the state

scores.rationale: The company is now a highly visible listed entity covered by Morgan Stanley, Motilal Oswal, PGIM and multiple funds, with a well-publicised IPO and merger — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: The first question comes from the line of Binay Singh from Morgan Stanley

scores.rationale: Gross margins are high and demand is steady with trust cited as the core driver, but the intangible does not convert into strong pricing power given price hikes limited to 2-3% annually.
scores.quote: the trust patients place in us and our ability to bring quality eye care to the doorstep

scores.rationale: Eye surgery is a certainty purchase and the company sells exactly that — clinical outcomes, accreditation, 360 international publications, and complex procedures like 1,150 corneal transplants — with price plainly secondary for the 72% who self-pay.
scores.quote: reinforcing our confidence in scaling expansion more aggressively, while continuing to deliver superior clinical outcomes

scores.rationale: The hub-and-spoke design exists to maximise accessibility — 269 facilities across 155 cities with primary clinics feeding secondary and tertiary hubs, handling ~10,000 walk-ins a day.
scores.quote: our ability to deliver quality eye care close to where patients live

scores.rationale: The customer base is overwhelmingly retail and self-paying (72% domestic cash), and the benefits offered — brand recall, trust and proximity — are precisely the intangible/assurance mix that fits retail rather than corporate buyers.
scores.quote: The domestic payer mix stood at 72% from cash, 22% from insurance and TPA and 6% from government schemes.

scores.rationale: The company is a fast, well-capitalised adopter of frontier ophthalmic technology (Femto robotic cataract up 87%, CATALYS, ELITA, SMILE) and built its own scalable HMS, but the core technology is bought from equipment vendors rather than proprietary.
scores.quote: robotic cataract surgeries, what we call as Femto Cataracts grew by a robust 87% year-on-year

scores.rationale: There is no two-sided network that strengthens with scale; the hub-and-spoke referral flow is an internal operating design, and patient demand is generated independently at each catchment.
scores.quote: we operate through something which we call a hub-and-spoke business model

scores.rationale: Physical reach is the durable advantage in a service where proximity is decisive — 269 facilities across 155 cities, one new opening a week in FY26, and 30 signed letters of intent giving visible runway no rival chain matches.
scores.quote: In FY '26, we have launched one new facility every week, adding our footprint across 26 new cities.

scores.rationale: Capex has stepped up sharply from ~INR50-60cr/yr guidance in FY23-24 to INR274cr in FY26 with ~INR300cr guided for FY27 for mechanization, but an analyst directly challenged that this has not yet expanded EBITDA and is pressuring return ratios, and management could only promise the payoff is 'coming couple of years'.
scores.quote: we have seen a noticeable step-up in capex intensity. However, this increased investment hasn't yet translated into a corresponding expansion in EBITDA

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or brand promotion spend in any excerpt.
No R&D spend, product pipeline or innovation programme is discussed anywhere in the calls.
No acquisitions, bolt-ons or inorganic activity mentioned across the 15 calls.
A question on 'distribution to' shareholders is cut off in the transcript and no dividend/buyback policy is articulated anywhere.
scores.quote: Any thoughts on distribution to

scores.rationale: The historically asset-light model is deteriorating — rising capex and depreciation without commensurate margin gain, and management concedes higher capex is now structurally 'the new norm' just to cope with labour shortage and complexity.
scores.quote: capex is going up, will go up because the required mechanization... this is the new norm

scores.rationale: Order book compounded from INR7,588cr (Nov-22) to INR13,144cr (Jun-24) to INR21,096cr (Mar-26) with FY26 inflow of INR10,257cr in a fragmented industry, showing real share capture even as revenue conversion lagged.
scores.quote: Net order book of the company as on 31st March 2026, is INR21,096.31 crores... Total order inflow during FY26 was INR10,257.39 crores

scores.rationale: Steady, self-funded expansion from a north-India base into the South (Bangalore, Hyderabad), 17 states and Nepal, executed as deliberate organic clustering rather than a land-grab, though it is domestic contracting not a travelling premium brand.
scores.quote: we have now started or restarted in Bangalore... And we have started our first project in Hyderbad

scores.rationale: Growth is volume/order-book-led while realisations have eroded — EBITDA margin fell from ~11% (FY23) to 9.5% (FY26) and management concedes the 13-14% 'glory days' are gone industry-wide, with escalation clauses (WPI pass-through) rather than pricing power protecting them.
scores.quote: the glory days of 13% to 14% are or the teens, so to say, are -- I don't think... we will be getting there

scores.rationale: Margins are near a cyclical trough (9.5%) with identifiable upturn drivers ahead — stable governments in Bihar/Bengal/Assam removing payment stress, GRAP mitigation, and a fast-moving Central Vista order insulated from NGT shutdowns.
scores.quote: all these areas have very stable governments... the cash strike or the payment issues that we had faced earlier in these states, we feel they are a thing of the past

scores.rationale: End market is in secular expansion — railway station redevelopment, airports, hospitals, institutional and data-centre buildings all cited as a robust multi-year pipeline, with bid pipeline and order inflow rising every year of the period.
scores.quote: pipeline is very robust... there are a number of infrastructure projects like railway station development, airports, hospitals, which are coming up

scores.rationale: Purely organic growth with no M&A, near-zero leverage (gross debt INR22cr against INR253cr cash plus INR587cr bank balance in Feb-26) and repeated refusal to chase volume, including walking away from residential and data-centre work.
scores.quote: Gross borrowing is INR22 crores, approximately... Cash balance is INR253 crores, and bank balance is INR587 crores

scores.rationale: Multi-year capability build is visible and consistent — in-house EPC disciplines developed over 4-5 years to qualify for larger tickets, and a mechanization bet taken two years before its payoff, culminating in the Central Vista win.
scores.quote: We have built in in-house capabilities that an EPC company has to have... this has been a conscious decision and we have been kind of building towards it over the last 4-5 years

scores.rationale: Calls are run by the Deputy MD and CFO with plain numbers and no promotional framing; the promoter-chairman never appears and there is no celebrity positioning across the four-year window.
scores.quote: Ahluwalia Contracts (India) Limited has announced its financial results for Q4 FY '26

scores.rationale: Talent is a chronic unmanaged weakness — perennial labour and skill shortage acknowledged since 2024, in-house training admitted to be at a 'very nascent stage', and skill levels described as deteriorating industry-wide.
scores.quote: training is also something that we've started, but that's in a very nascent stage

scores.rationale: Consistently owns misses in detail rather than deflecting — itemised the 6.58% margin collapse in Q1FY25 including NCLT write-offs, cut FY26 guidance from 15-20% to 10-15% on the record, and told an analyst plainly the old margin structure will not return.
scores.quote: there are a couple of write-offs totaling Rs. 6.20 crores where couple of our clients have been taken to NCLT. So, we have had to put in those write-offs

scores.rationale: Management is credible and candid, but the multi-year record separates talk from delivery poorly — 12% margins were promised in Nov-2022 and 'maintained' for years, yet FY26 closed at 9.52%, so skill should not be read from the strong order-book optics.
scores.quote: So basically, we are saying we are on track to go to a 12% targeted range, probably we'll exit the year at that level, around 12%?

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position; work is won project-by-project through competitive L1 tendering with no aftermarket or services annuity attached.
scores.quote: since our projects are L1 and we'll have limited room

scores.rationale: Zero switching costs — each contract is re-bid, and even long-standing clients like DLF or Signature Global award individual projects, with the company confirming it did not even bid for one of them.
scores.quote: that's why we are not associated with that job, nor have we bid for that job

scores.rationale: Mixed structure — the government segment is crowded and price-driven, while the complex private high-rise segment has few qualified players, giving partial but unstable oligopoly benefits.
scores.quote: There are only a handful of contractors in the private sector side. The competition is less

scores.rationale: Barriers are weak and pricing irrational — management repeatedly cites high competitive intensity forcing conservative bidding, and margins have compressed industry-wide from low teens to single digits.
scores.quote: we have been very conservative because the competitive intensity remains high

scores.rationale: Weak peers are visibly donating share — management claims consistently better margins than close peers in its own comparisons, and some clients/competitors in the ecosystem have gone into NCLT.
scores.quote: I have a peer comparison in front of me. I think we've beaten the margins of some of my closest peers, smaller and bigger than us

scores.rationale: It is a deliberately narrow niche (buildings and factories only, no roads/residential focus), but it is not ignored — calls are hosted by Ambit, ICICI, JM, Nuvama, Dolat and attended by institutional investors like Marcellus.
scores.quote: since we are only in buildings and factories

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power; margins are set by tender rates and input inflation, with protection coming only from WPI escalation clauses and raw-material pass-throughs, not brand.
scores.quote: all heavy material like cement, steel, raw material, the basic price of procurement is a pass-through

scores.rationale: Private clients demonstrably pay up for reliability and on-time delivery, which is the stated reason for the deliberate shift toward private-sector work at better rates.
scores.quote: There is greater demand for timely delivery, quality delivery... The rates that we are able to get are far better than the government projects

scores.rationale: Deliberate geographic clustering gives unusual client proximity and overhead leverage — roughly 20 million sq ft executed within a 15-20 km radius in NCR, with multiple projects in each of 17 states.
scores.quote: within a radius of about 15 to 20 kilometers, we would be doing nearly 20 million square feet

scores.rationale: Customer base is entirely corporate/government where reliability and TCO are the right levers and the private mix has risen past 60%, but there is no switching-cost lock-in to convert that trust into repeat economics.
scores.quote: I think over 60% of the order book is of private clients

scores.rationale: Some genuine capability depth — in-house design-build across multiple disciplines and a mechanization programme — but it is catch-up investment forced by labour shortage rather than a proprietary, high-R&D edge.
scores.quote: We have different disciplines where we have developed expertise other than core and shell also

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is discussed anywhere in the calls.
Execution reach across 17 states with clustered sites is a real operating advantage, but it is replicable scale rather than a distribution/service network rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: in each of the states that we are working in, 17 states that we are working in, we have multiple projects

scores.rationale: Sustained growth capex (50k t mill-lining plant, 80k t grinding media at ~Rs 250cr, Rs 65cr composite-rubber liner line, Ghana/China plants) was funded and built, but incremental ROIC has been poor — volumes are flat at ~258k tons against 436k capacity and utilisation is only ~55%, with 24k tons of Welcast capacity actually shut.
scores.quote: Current capacity utilization this year is about 55% overall.

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any excerpt.

R&D is in-house and has produced a genuinely new product suite (composite/rubber liners developed internally with 6-8 pilot trials, then the 'new generation discharge system' that after two years of refinement delivered a marquee South American win) though commercial payoff has been slow.
scores.quote: It's all in-house... we have done more than six to eight trials

scores.rationale: No acquisitions are discussed across the excerpts; the only portfolio action is the closure of the Welcast Steels subsidiary, which is not an M&A judgement.

A Rs 500cr buyback plus dividends were executed in FY25, but net cash still climbed from Rs 2,065cr (2022) to ~Rs 4,300cr (2026) with capex needs of only Rs 100-150cr, indicating no coherent policy for deploying or returning the accumulating idle cash.
scores.quote: We have also done a buyback; Board approved a buyback of Rs. 500 crores... Our net cash stands at about Rs. 3,500 crores

scores.rationale: The business is asset-heavy and getting heavier — a foundry running at 55% utilisation, ~120 days of working capital with inventory further inflated by long transit times, and a Rs 4,300cr cash block against Rs 4,355cr of revenue, so asset turn is low despite the moat.
scores.quote: Currently, whatever 4,36,000 tons capacity, in front of that 2,58,000 tons our production is done.

scores.rationale: The runway is genuine and large (an 800k-1m ton gold/copper market versus ~250k tons of total sales) but actual share capture has stalled — FY26 sales of 258k tons versus 255k in FY25, well short of the 25-35k tons/year conversion promised in 2022.
scores.quote: we remain optimistic of doing 30,000 tons of additional tonnage this year and then continuing that pace of 25,000 tons to 35,000 tons each year thereafter

scores.rationale: Global reach is real (140 countries, subsidiaries in Brazil, Canada, South Africa) but the localisation response to protectionism — Ghana and China plants — has slipped repeatedly and is now explicitly deprioritised.
scores.quote: Ghana as well as China are on a bit slowdown mode

scores.rationale: With volumes flat, essentially all revenue and record-profit growth came from realisation moving Rs 150 → Rs 165-178/kg on richer casting mix and rupee depreciation, plus a demonstrated ability to pass through raw material and freight inflation.
scores.quote: the combination of the rupee weakening income on account of currency and the product mix has translated to a realization per kilogram of about INR178

scores.rationale: Mining end-markets are described as buoyant with metals surging rather than near a cyclical bottom, and management explicitly says its fortunes are not tied to the size of the pie.
scores.quote: We are not linked to growing that pie, right? That is not what we are focused on or really affects our fortunes.

scores.rationale: The structural driver is credible and permanent — falling ore grades mean more ore must be ground per unit of metal, and copper supply must roughly double over 20 years — though four years of flat tonnage show AIA has not yet monetised it.
scores.quote: the world has mined x amount of copper... that amount of copper will needed to be mined in the next 20 years... copper looks to be in a structural bull run

scores.rationale: Consistently organic, debt-free with Rs 4,300cr net cash, no acquisitions, capex and renewables investment continued straight through the container/freight downturn, and an underperforming subsidiary plant was shut rather than propped up.
scores.quote: we've closed our plant in... Welcast Steels, and that reflected 24,000 tons of capacity

scores.rationale: The same forged-to-chrome conversion thesis has been pursued without deviation across four years of freight shocks, container shortages and antidumping cases, including two years of iterative work with a single customer before the discharge-system breakthrough.
scores.quote: over 2 years, we work with that customers gets sharpening and refining our solution, doing multiple rounds of supply. And finally, we've gotten that... win

scores.rationale: Management is low-key and substance-oriented — refusing to hype the first chrome win, declining volume guidance rather than promising numbers, and repeatedly asking analysts not to extrapolate.
scores.quote: A lot of people then ask us, will that mean 100,000 tons coming up?... we don't want to be in a situation where we go ahead of ourselves

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development, succession or internal leadership pipeline in the excerpts.

Management names problems plainly, withdraws guidance rather than dressing it up, admits its own earlier assessment was wrong, and separates one-off currency and tax benefits from underlying performance unprompted.
scores.quote: It's wrong to say that, no, there is no problem... it is not as simple as we were earlier thinking

scores.rationale: Record FY26 EBITDA and PAT are flattered by factors outside management skill — Rs 65cr of FX sitting inside EBITDA (4-5% of margin), Rs 67-83cr quarterly treasury income on the cash pile, and a one-off Rs 25-30cr tax benefit — while the core operating metric, tonnage, has not grown in four years.
scores.quote: There is INR65 crores currency that's sitting in the EBITDA for this quarter and which is about 4% or 5% in EBITDA

scores.rationale: Management claims a solution-level monopoly in the customer's mind for ball-mill throughput problems, and the credibility is supported by a real proof-of-concept win rather than assertion alone, though high-chrome media itself has established competitors.
scores.quote: AIA is the only company in the world which is offering this solution for ball mills

scores.rationale: Switching costs are real and two-sided — conversions require multi-year trials and design work, and once a mine converts, the successful reference immediately produced a follow-on order for the customer's second mine.
scores.quote: after the successful trial in one of their mines, they have immediately also given us the order for the second mine conversion

scores.rationale: The high-chrome niche is concentrated but the end customers are very large global miners with real negotiating power, and pricing is constantly attacked via antidumping and countervailing duty proceedings in the US and Brazil.
scores.quote: the pricing, which was already and always creating headaches about antidumping and all those issues

scores.rationale: Barriers are broad (design, pattern-making, metallurgy, service ecosystem — not just casting capacity), no new entrants are cited, ownership is stable, and management deliberately refuses to compete on price.
scores.quote: I do not think it's going to be a price discussion at all... surely not a price

scores.rationale: A large pool of weak incumbents exists — local forged-media producers across an 800k-1m ton gold/copper market — but four years of flat tonnage show the donated share has not actually transferred at the promised pace.
scores.quote: there is a large market. 800,000 to 1 million ton market for gold and copper and all mines facing critical issues

scores.rationale: The business is a deliberately narrow, unglamorous mill-internals niche that management insists on keeping specialised rather than commoditised, drawing little competitive or capital attention.
scores.quote: the focus remains niche... and not me-too kind of product

scores.rationale: Demand is steady and gross margins are healthy (raw material ~44% of sales, 28% operating EBITDA), but pricing power derives from measurable process economics rather than image or taste, so the intangible lever is largely absent.
scores.quote: Significant efficiency related solution, efficiency improvement, massive cost reduction due to improved throughputs

scores.rationale: Customers explicitly buy certainty of process outcome — throughput, power savings and recovery — and management states the sale cycle turns on confidence and willingness to trust a new solution, not on price.
scores.quote: the conversion is going to be linked to their comfort and confidence, and ability to be the willingness to try a new solution... surely not a price

scores.rationale: Direct customer intimacy is strong (in-house design, metallurgy and service interfacing, local warehousing), but accessibility is structurally impaired by shipping from India — 30-40 day lead times stretching to three months and containers arriving four months late.
scores.quote: we were without containers, what we wanted in June is coming to us in end of October

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate/industrial and the pitch is correctly matched to it — TCO and reliability (throughput, power, recovery, down-process benefits) plus multi-year trial-based lock-in rather than brand appeal.
scores.quote: our endeavor is to improve throughput, reduce power consumption and bring a whole host of operational benefits for the customer

scores.rationale: The edge is multi-product and design-led — metal, composite and rubber liners plus the discharge system, validated by a hard throughput and power result in abusive large-mill conditions — though R&D intensity is not quantified and the payoff cycle is very long.
scores.quote: we implemented our solution of the discharge system... And it brought in material benefits, which is throughput improvement power reduction

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network is described; the reference-customer effect cited is a credibility mechanism, not a network effect.

Global reach across 140 countries with local subsidiaries and stocking is genuine, but distribution is a repeated liability rather than an advantage — container shortages, volatile freight and protectionist duties have directly stalled conversions since 2022.
scores.quote: shipping remains to be a proxy for global geopolitical uncertainty... customers that migrate to our solution will be exposed to the global supply chain

scores.rationale: Capex has risen from ~Rs 200cr (FY23) to Rs 330cr (FY26) with FY27 guided at Rs 400cr of which only Rs 150cr is maintenance, and a new Pithampur liquid line was commissioned, all while ROCE stayed 33-34%, though absolute growth capex remains modest versus Rs 5,453cr revenue.
scores.quote: We expect capex to increase to around Rs. 400 crores in the FY 2027, which includes Rs. 150 crores of maintenance and balance for new capacity expansion.

scores.rationale: Brand/promotion spend is repeatedly flagged as a deliberate P&L investment (other expenses +24%) alongside field expansion, and it coincides with IPM outperformance and rank improvement, but it is never quantified separately from personnel.
scores.quote: These expenses represent our continued strategic investment in products, brand and people across our branded generic portfolio.

scores.rationale: R&D held steadily at 5-6% of revenue (Rs 54cr in Q1FY23 to Rs 252cr FY26) and converted into 8 US launches in 15 months driving 49% US growth plus 26 India launches including five first-in-country, a high conversion rate per rupee spent.
scores.quote: This performance was driven by 8 new launches over the past 15 months... registering a robust growth of 49%.

scores.rationale: No acquisitions were made across the five years — the company is only now signalling a Rs 1,000cr+ acquisition ambition with no track record to judge, while explicitly ruling out unrelated-business deals.
scores.quote: we are actively looking for the acquisition also. And as it was there in the news that we have Rs. 1,000 crores plus for that.

scores.rationale: A consistent 60-80% payout of PAT via dividends and buybacks over 4-5 years plus a Rs 350cr interim dividend in FY26 shows a coherent policy, though FY26 payout dropped to 44% and is now explicitly contingent on the acquisition plan.
scores.quote: we have maintained both payout in terms of dividend and buyback in last 4, 5 years in a range between 60% to 80%. This year, we have given a payout of about 44%.

scores.rationale: ROCE of 33-34% and ROE of 25-26% on modest capex with inventory cut from 72 to 63 days indicates good capital efficiency, though receivables ballooned from 94 to 125 days after the factoring switch.
scores.quote: return on capital employed stood at 33% and return on net worth at 25%, underscoring our position among the best performing companies in the industry.

scores.rationale: Sustained share capture from a non-dominant base: IPM rank improved from 29 (2022) to 28 to 24 (MAT Mar 2026), growth consistently ahead of IPM (13% vs 10%), plus explicit share gains in existing US products.
scores.quote: Ajanta is now among the top 25 companies in the Indian pharmaceutical market... Our ranking has improved to rank 24th against rank 26th last year.

scores.rationale: Genuine multi-geography build-out (Asia, Africa, US, a 26-country GLP-1 tie-up, LatAm under evaluation) but execution has been uneven, with Asia declining 1% in FY26 against a double-digit internal plan.
scores.quote: we are also looking to expand into the new territories, possibly into the Latin America

scores.rationale: Growth is led by volume and new launches rather than price/mix — FY23 India split was 7% price, 6% volume, 3% new products, and by FY26 the boast is volume growth at 2x IPM, though the chronic-therapy tilt improves mix.
scores.quote: We continue to exceed volume growth by 2x to IPM and new launches by 39%.

scores.rationale: The US price-erosion cycle bottomed around FY23 and the company is now at the top of that upswing (49% FY26 growth), with management itself guiding deceleration, so the cyclical position is late rather than early.
scores.quote: the growth probably will not be in the similar line of what we have seen in current year. But I think we should be able to post double-digit growth for sure.

scores.rationale: End markets are in secular expansion — Indian pharma growing ~10% p.a. with a chronic-therapy shift, plus emerging Asia/Africa and the new GLP-1 category, supporting 17-21% company revenue growth to cross Rs 5,000cr.
scores.quote: revenue surpassing Rs. 5,000 crores and net profit crossing Rs. 1,000 crores

scores.rationale: Wholly organic growth over the period with counter-cyclical investment in MRs and products through soft quarters and near-debt-free operations, but the newly announced Rs 1,000cr acquisition intent is an untested departure.
scores.quote: we are still going to get the same EBITDA margin... in spite of all the expenses or investment, which we are doing in branded generic markets

scores.rationale: Promoter-managers show consistent multi-year discipline — refusing launches they lack conviction in, accepting 1.5-2 year MR payback periods, and building gynaecology/nephrology patiently rather than chasing quarterly optics.
scores.quote: I do not expect to cross it or to launch brands where we are not very confident of the future growth potential of those segments

scores.rationale: Same low-key promoter-CFO trio across all five calls, plain factual commentary, declining to disclose region-level field size or segment EBITDA, with no personality-driven narrative.
scores.quote: being a proprietary kind of information we are not giving out the region level field size

scores.rationale: Heavy, deliberate investment in field talent (5,680 people, 300 MRs added in FY26, PCPM tracked at 3.7 lakh vs 4-4.5 lakh steady state) with stated productivity integration, but no evidence of a formal leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: The newly onboarded teams are being integrated with a clear focus on productivity and effective field execution.

scores.rationale: Repeatedly flags its own misses and caveats favourable optics — warning that Q1FY23 growth looked 'elevated' on a low base, disclosing Asia was below internal plan, explaining the forex/EBITDA accounting distortion, and admitting freight costs are absorbed not passed on.
scores.quote: Asia, on the other hand, remained modestly below our original plan due to softer traction in certain markets.

scores.rationale: The record survives halo scrutiny reasonably well because management itself separates skill from optics — rejecting margin-expansion narratives, disclosing that forex and a seasonal flu product aided results, and reporting degrowth openly.
scores.quote: guiding towards that kind of expansion of 30% or plus probably will not be the right metrics to look

scores.rationale: Some brand strength exists (three brands in IPM top 500, first-to-market launches, top-10 in all covered therapies) but nothing approaching a monopoly position in the customer's mind or a captive aftermarket.
scores.quote: we are fifth largest in IPM and amongst top-10 in all our therapeutic segments

scores.rationale: Branded-generic prescriber stickiness gives modest lock-in, but the calls describe competitive therapy segments and a US business exposed to open price erosion, with no evidence of regional monopoly or switching costs.
scores.quote: despite the severe price erosion, which we have seen in the US market

scores.rationale: Core markets are fragmented and buyer-powerful — US generics saw 15-18% price erosion with distributor concentration, and the IPM is a market where Ajanta ranks only 24th, far from a stable oligopoly.
scores.quote: because of the severe price erosion, which last year was 15% to 18% it has adversely impacted the EBITDA margin of the US business

scores.rationale: Selective focus on complex/limited-competition products and stable promoter ownership offer some protection, but the industry shows recurring discount-driven erosion and 'plethora of launches taking place across the industry' in its India target therapies.
scores.quote: there are multiple new product opportunities including fix dose combinations. So we are also in the race

scores.rationale: Consistently takes share from weaker players — outgrowing IPM by 28-32%, gaining two dermatology ranks, and winning market share in existing US molecules and African territories.
scores.quote: gain in market share in few existing products

scores.rationale: Operates in under-followed niches (ophthalmology 30-31% of India sales, West/East Africa, Central Asia) with a deliberately sparse disclosure style and modest analyst following relative to larger pharma peers.
scores.quote: Ajanta's Asia business remains focused on Middle East, South-East Asia and Central Asia.

scores.rationale: Branded-generic positioning sustains 77-79% gross margins and allowed a 7% price increase to be pushed through in FY23, indicating real prescriber-level brand pull, though not premium-consumer-brand strength.
scores.quote: Gross margins stood at 79% for the quarter and 78% for the full year.

scores.rationale: The US business explicitly wins on reliability rather than price — repeatedly described as preferred partner status built on supply reliability, quality and execution, which is what drove 49% growth and share gains.
scores.quote: We continue to be a preferred partner for distributors and customers, anchored in reliable supply, strong quality standards and disciplined execution.

scores.rationale: A 5,680-strong field force including 3,750 India MRs delivering Rs 3.7 lakh PCPM gives direct, intensive doctor-level intimacy that is the company's primary go-to-market asset and the reason coverage keeps expanding.
scores.quote: we added around 300 medical representatives across our therapeutic areas, taking our total field force to approximately 3,750 MRs

scores.rationale: Benefit type is well matched to customer — brand/detailing intangibles for retail-facing prescribers in India, Asia and Africa (68-70% of revenue), and reliability/execution for corporate US distributors.
scores.quote: we have a very strong ground presence through our field force and promo plans

scores.rationale: R&D at only 5% of revenue is aimed at generic ANDAs and fixed-dose combinations rather than a differentiated tech platform, and the GLP-1 opportunity is being accessed by in-licensing finished product from Biocon, not internal capability.
scores.quote: they will be supplying the finished product. They have the finished products. They have all the required data

scores.rationale: No evidence in any of the five calls of a two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic.

The multi-country field force is the durable, hard-to-replicate asset — it is precisely why Biocon granted exclusive GLP-1 rights across 23 of 26 countries, and it underpins the launch-and-scale model in Asia, Africa and India.
scores.quote: we have tied up with them for 26 countries where 23 is exclusive tie-up with us... where we have a very strong ground presence through our field force

scores.rationale: Sustained growth capex on genuinely new capacity — dedicated injectable, Penem, Baddi (oncology/steroidal), Jammu — is ramping and EU/ANVISA-accredited, but incremental returns are still unproven with CDMO FY26 EBITDA up only 2.9% on 8.6% revenue growth.
scores.quote: our newer facilities including the dedicated injectable plant, the Penem facility and the new plant in Baddi are all progressing through their respective ramp up curves

scores.rationale: Brand spend is confined to the small Akumentis field force where management explicitly deprioritised topline for margin, so A&P has protected profitability but not demonstrably built brand equity (domestic branded revenue +2.9% in FY26).
scores.quote: top-line growth was not a key driver for us. It was how do we improve our profitability in this business

scores.rationale: R&D consistently converts into commercialised output — 1,000 cumulative DCGI approvals, 27 in one quarter versus 31 in the whole prior year, 24 patents filed in a quarter, triple-layer tablets, first EU dossier approval — at ~INR100 crore+ per year for three years, and management directly links it to gross-margin gains.
scores.quote: we have been investing over INR100 crores in our R&D, which is a result of which we can -- at a larger base as well, we can gradually move up our gross margins

scores.rationale: The Parabolic/Pure and Cure API acquisition was a distressed, not-already-strong asset that has drained EBITDA for years (FY26 API EBITDA still negative INR40 crore) and management itself called it a miss, though current M&A filters sound disciplined.
scores.quote: On the API, this was a year of miss, honestly.

scores.rationale: A first meaningful distribution (INR1 final plus INR2 special dividend) was declared, but INR1,682 crore of cash sits undeployed with no buyback and only exploratory acquisition talk, so no coherent distribution policy is yet evident.
scores.quote: The Board has also recommended final dividend for the year FY 2026 for INR1 per equity share and a special dividend of INR2 per equity share.

scores.rationale: This is an asset-heavy business — 11+ formulation units, 49 billion units of capacity, multiple new plants in multi-year ramp — generating only ~INR4,359 crore revenue on a cost-plus model, so turnover is not the asset-light/moat combination sought.
scores.quote: We have 11 units operational for formulation CDMO business with capacity of over 49 billion units annually

scores.rationale: Clear share capture — double-digit and 25%+ volume variance against an industry growing 1%-1.5% — though the runway is limited by an already-dominant 30%+ CDMO share.
scores.quote: the overall IPM is still growing at 1%, 1.5%, but we think that this is a sustained growth

scores.rationale: Credible, milestone-by-milestone international build-out (EU GMP for Plants 1 and 2, first EU dossier approval, EUR35m/yr contract to 2032 with EUR100m received upfront, Zambia $25m, ANVISA Brazil, Russia GMP), but commercial scale is still deferred to FY28 and international branded revenue was flat in FY26.
scores.quote: the annual run rate for the orders will be in the tune of EUR 35 million, and the contract is till December of 2032

scores.rationale: Growth is volume-led with structurally negative pricing — a cost-plus model passing through 20%-25% API price declines — with mix improvement acting only as a margin offset, the inverse of pricing/mix-led growth.
scores.quote: the price variance has been a negative 3.5% on an average in the last few quarters

scores.rationale: The company sits at the trough of a multi-year API price cycle that is now visibly turning, with prices up high single digits and cephalosporin decline moderating, giving an identifiable upturn ahead.
scores.quote: Due to the current ongoing global geopolitical situation, the API prices have slightly gone up, single high-digits

scores.rationale: Outsourced Indian formulation manufacturing is structurally expanding as regulatory enforcement pushes volume toward compliant large manufacturers, though the underlying IPM volume growth has been near-zero for two years.
scores.quote: We believe this reflects a structural strength supported by growing customer preference for compliant manufacturers.

scores.rationale: Debt cut from INR418 crore to INR213 crore, net cash of INR1,682 crore, organic capex maintained through a severe downturn, and explicit price/fit discipline on deploying the cash — offset by the earlier Parabolic misadventure.
scores.quote: the idea is to remain cognizant of what we are buying, at what price we are buying, and whether or not it will be incremental to our current business

scores.rationale: Multi-year regulated-market ambition articulated in 2024 has been executed step by step through a bad cycle — EU GMP since 2022, audits, filings, plant upgrades — with each stated milestone landing roughly on schedule across eight calls.
scores.quote: continue to invest for the future to ensure long-term sustainable growth

scores.rationale: The promoter MDs speak briefly and factually and delegate detail to the CFO and strategy head, with no self-promotion or celebrity framing across all eight calls.
scores.quote: Namaskar everyone and thanks for joining us on this call.

scores.rationale: Capability is being added mainly through senior external hires (CDMO CEO, IT and finance executives) plus HR digitalisation, with no evidence presented of a systematic internal leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: We strengthened our leadership team this quarter with addition of senior executives in IT, finance.

scores.rationale: Management cuts guidance openly, names the API business a miss, and admits it does not fully understand its own volume surge — though early on it declined to break out segment economics analysts requested.
scores.quote: honestly, what it is driving is still to be thought through and looked out

scores.rationale: There is little halo to strip out — FY26 revenue grew only 5.8% and PAT fell — and management attributes swings largely to external API pricing rather than claiming skill, so results and skill remain hard to separate.
scores.quote: whatever is the cost of input material gets passed on as part of our CDMO contracts

scores.rationale: Akums holds a monopoly-like position in the minds of Indian pharma customers as the default domestic CDMO, with 30%+ share and 26 of the top 30 companies as clients.
scores.quote: the largest India-focused pharmaceutical CDMO with over 30% market share

scores.rationale: Product-specific DCGI registrations, tech transfer and repeated client audits create real switching costs, evidenced by 15+ year MNC relationships and volume growth coming almost entirely from existing customers.
scores.quote: this is primarily led from existing customers only. So, this is not new geographies or new customers

scores.rationale: The Indian CDMO field is fragmented rather than a stable oligopoly, and the transparent cost-plus model leaves large pharma customers with clear negotiating power over conversion margins fixed in the 14%-15% band.
scores.quote: a 14% to 15% margin is what we usually deliver in this business. That should be the zip code in which we operate

scores.rationale: Rising regulatory enforcement and costly global accreditations raise the entry bar and are visibly shifting volume to compliant players, with stable promoter-family ownership, though margins show no pricing rationality premium.
scores.quote: there might be some play off enforced regulations being stricter

scores.rationale: Non-compliant smaller manufacturers are the identified donators, with Akums explicitly attributing broad-based volume gains to stricter enforcement and customer flight to compliant manufacturers.
scores.quote: growing customer preference for compliant manufacturers

scores.rationale: Post-IPO the company is closely followed by Ambit, Citi, Fidelity, HSBC, Franklin Templeton and ICICI, so it is neither ignored by capital nor under the radar.
scores.quote: the next question is from the line of Madhav from Fidelity

scores.rationale: There is no image- or taste-driven pricing power: revenue realisation moves mechanically with API prices under a full pass-through model, and gross margins of ~37% are industrial rather than premium.
scores.quote: Every purchase order, it's a complete pass through to the customers whether it's a inflated price or a subdued price of the API

scores.rationale: The core customer proposition is certainty — regulatory compliance, audit-passing quality systems and 15+ years of serving MNC KRA standards — and management credits demand shifts directly to buyers seeking compliant, reliable manufacturing.
scores.quote: we already serve large Indian customers and MNCs Indians markets who themselves have a strict KRA sheet of how they operate

scores.rationale: One-stop breadth is a genuine convenience advantage — 60+ dosage forms, 4,000+ formulations and 1,500 clients served annually — supported by a 1,500-strong field force on the branded side.
scores.quote: we have commercialized over 4,000 formulations across our 60-plus dosage forms

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is correctly matched to a corporate customer base — reliability, compliance and registration-driven lock-in for pharma clients — with the small retail-facing branded arm a secondary contributor.
scores.quote: 26 out of top 30 in India pharma market being our partners

scores.rationale: A real multi-product formulation-technology edge exists — 20-25 in-house platform technologies, a granted patent, 24 filings in one quarter and first-time triple-layer tablets — but R&D intensity of ~2.5% of sales is modest for a deep tech moat.
scores.quote: we have technologies which are almost 20-25 technologies, which we have in-house, which help us to get the product faster to the market

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is discussed anywhere across the eight calls.

Distribution is largely the clients' responsibility in the CDMO model, and the company's own reach — a 1,500-person field force and third-party distributors — is unremarkable, with no field force at all in its new European market.
scores.quote: we don't still have a field force in Europe, right? This is still based upon large companies or large distributors

scores.rationale: Sustained growth capex — Dahej/Ankleshwar brownfields plus Solapur greenfield taking capacity from 1,198 KL in FY24 to a planned 2,690 KL by FY28, ~INR 472cr spent over two years, all internally funded — but incremental returns are unproven since revenue CAGR was only 5.7% over the same period and capex was repeatedly deferred/downsized.
scores.quote: The capacity we are adding today will take us from 1,198 KL in FY 24 to a planned 2,690 KL by FY28

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotional spend across any of the calls — it is a B2B API/CDMO business with no consumer brand.

R&D held steadily at ~3–3.6% of sales and demonstrably converts into output — 611 DMF/CEP filings, 176 molecules, 11 new products and 49 new customers in FY26, plus a 28-product high-potency pipeline and a new Taloja R&D centre — though the high-potency portfolio contributes almost nothing to revenue until 2028 patent expiries.
scores.quote: R&D expenditure ... for the full financial year 2026, it was INR 91 crores, again, 3.6% of our sales

scores.rationale: No acquisitions have been executed in the period; management says it is actively looking for platform-adjacent bolt-ons and explicitly refuses to deploy cash carelessly, so there is discipline but no track record to score positively.
scores.quote: we are not just going to do things willy nilly. I mean, it's hard-earned money and we are going to make sure that it's deployed well

scores.rationale: Distribution policy is coherently explained but deliberately shrunk — dividend cut from ~INR 21.50/share to just INR 61cr over two years while INR 451cr of cash was retained as a 'war chest' for capex, and no buybacks were undertaken at any valuation.
scores.quote: the dividend payout may not be as high as what it used to be in the past ... it will not be as high as what you have seen in the past

scores.rationale: This is an asset-heavy multi-plant API manufacturer with revenue of INR 2,552cr against continuous multi-hundred-crore capex and a stated asset-turn ambition of only 1.3–1.5x sales per rupee invested, offset by genuinely high returns (~30% ROCE) and regulatory-filing protection.
scores.quote: the revenue potential of new capex at 1.3x to 1.5x the amount of money invested

scores.rationale: Evidence of real customer capture — 49 new customers added in FY26 to a base of ~900 and non-GPL revenue growing 13–16% versus 6.9% headline — but total growth is only high single digit, so share gain is incremental rather than emphatic.
scores.quote: We have also added 49 new customers during FY26, taking our total base of customers to about 900

scores.rationale: Broad-based, credibly executed geographic delivery with launches in Europe, China, LATAM and Russia and growth across Europe, Japan, LATAM, RoW and India, reducing dependence on the erstwhile parent from 41% to 29% of revenue.
scores.quote: we have had launches in Europe, in China, in LATAM and Russia. So, these all these launches have contributed very significantly to the margin

scores.rationale: Growth and the entire 360bp EBITDA margin expansion are explicitly mix- and launch-led (chronic CVS/CNS, CDMO up to 7% of sales, high-value differentiated products) rather than volume-led, though underlying base pricing erodes 4–4.5% annually.
scores.quote: driven by a favorable product mix, disciplined cost management, operational efficiencies and an increasing focus on high-value differentiated products

scores.rationale: The company passed through the API destocking trough (weak FY24, Japan 'bottomed out') and is now in an identifiable upturn with CDMO revenue up 85% YoY and record quarterly revenue, so much of the cyclical recovery is already visible rather than ahead.
scores.quote: our CDMO segment has made a strong recovery, delivering an exceptional performance in Q3, with revenue growth of 100% QoQ and 85.3% YoY

scores.rationale: End market has genuine secular support — ageing population, rising chronic disease, sustained healthcare spend — reinforced by China+1 supply-chain de-risking and the Biosecure Act favouring Indian API suppliers.
scores.quote: Demand remains resilient, supported by an aging population, rising chronic disease prevalence and sustained healthcare spending

scores.rationale: Consistently organic, net debt free across all 15 quarters, capex fully funded by internal accruals, capacity built in a calibrated way to avoid under-absorption, and investment continued through the FY24 downturn with no large M&A.
scores.quote: our capacity expansions are going to be calibrated, because there's no point in building too much capacity and not utilizing it. You just create more under-absorption

scores.rationale: Rawjee and Mistry held course through a full change of promoter (Glenmark to Nirma), the PLI expiry, a GPCB closure notice and a plant fire, rebuilding EBITDA margin from 28% to 33.6% — but the 13–15% external growth repeatedly guided from 2022 became a 5.7% revenue CAGR, so tenacity on profitability outran delivery on growth.
scores.quote: we were also wondering whether we will be able to bring it back. But we have been able to do that. And it's happened steadily

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently technical and understated — the same small team (MD, CFO, comms GM) presenting plant-level detail, price erosion and yields without promotional framing or celebrity positioning.
scores.quote: I would say it's fairly stable. I mean, on our entire bucket, we are guiding to 4%-4.5% margin erosion

scores.rationale: Employees appear only as a cost line (headcount build at Dahej, employee cost under 10% of revenue, performance bonuses accrued); there is no discussion of talent development or a leadership pipeline in any call.

Repeatedly discloses bad news early and unprompted — pre-warned investors of the PLI cliff, volunteered the Gujarat Pollution Control Board closure notice in opening remarks, quantified the INR 20cr fire loss and INR 31cr forex gain, and openly cut capex guidance from INR 600cr to INR 450cr and admitted the Solapur delay and downsizing.
scores.quote: we got a closure notice from the Gujarat Pollution Control Board ... while the situation is not good and it has come as a surprise because we have been in compliance all along

scores.rationale: Record 33.6% margins are genuinely skill-driven in part (yields, energy, next-generation processes), but a sober read notes revenue grew only 5.7% CAGR, INR 31cr of forex gain flattered FY26, and CDMO's rebound is cyclical — so results should not be read as pure management quality.
scores.quote: between FY24 to FY26, our revenue CAGR stood at 5.7%, while EBITDA CAGR during the same period was 15.8%

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position — generic APIs face routine annual price erosion that management describes as universal in the industry, and it competes across a 176-molecule basket rather than owning a customer's mind.
scores.quote: we are seeing normal erosion. And that's very, very common in our business. I mean every company faces this kind of challenge

scores.rationale: Real regulatory switching costs exist — customers must file the supplier's DMF/CEP and run exhibit batches and variation filings to change source (611 filings globally), plus a captive ~29% share of revenue from the erstwhile parent.
scores.quote: We have supplied the validation quantities, which were then taken by them for exhibit batches and variation filing

scores.rationale: The generic API market is fragmented and price-competitive with Chinese supply pressure; management concedes ongoing 4–4.5% price erosion and must pass through cost increases by negotiating with customers, indicating no oligopolistic pricing control.
scores.quote: we are in touch with our customers to give them that view and most customers are agreeable to take on that added cost

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are meaningful (FDA/regulatory inspections, DMF/CEP filings, multi-year plant qualification — Solapur will not serve regulated markets until late FY28), pricing behaviour is rational with no discount war, and ownership is stable under Nirma.
scores.quote: if we can trigger an inspection in a year's time, then by late FY'28, we should see regulated products happening from Solapur

scores.rationale: Supply-chain de-risking away from China and the Biosecure Act create identifiable weak incumbents to take share from, which management says is already playing out in its favour.
scores.quote: that full Biosecure act ... it's benefit to Indian companies especially ones that are catering to the more innovative side of business is beginning to play out as well

scores.rationale: Operates a deliberately unglamorous mid-volume/high-value niche in complex chronic APIs and high-potency oncology molecules, and explicitly declines the crowded, capital-attracting clinical-phase CDMO segment.
scores.quote: we have to offer ... mid volume and high value products

scores.rationale: Gross margins of 58–60% are high and demand is steady, but the pricing power comes from product complexity and mix rather than image or taste, and the base portfolio still erodes 4–4.5% a year.
scores.quote: Gross margins for FY 26 stood at 58.2%, up 350 basis points

scores.rationale: Customers are buying regulatory reliability and quality compliance — management frames the industry shift explicitly this way — though the GPCB closure notice and the Dahej fire show the assurance is not unbreachable.
scores.quote: tighter regulatory scrutiny and supply chain de-risking are reinforcing the need for quality compliance and reliable partners

scores.rationale: A base of ~900 direct customers with 49 added in FY26 implies decent commercial reach, but there is no evidence of a distinctive distribution, service-accessibility or sales-force advantage in any call.
scores.quote: taking our total base of customers to about 900

scores.rationale: Purely corporate customers, and the benefit set is correctly matched — regulatory qualification lock-in, supply reliability and cost pass-through negotiation rather than any consumer-style intangible.
scores.quote: Pricing with Glenmark Pharma has always been at arm's length

scores.rationale: Genuine process-chemistry depth — complex iron complexes, oncology and a 28-molecule high-potency pipeline with a $70bn TAM, plus next-generation processes deliberately lined up to defend margins against price erosion — but R&D intensity of 3.6% is moderate and the high-potency edge is unmonetised until 2028.
scores.quote: on those products where we are likely to see a price erosion, we do have the next generation process lined up. So, margins are not going to get impacted

scores.rationale: Network effects are never discussed and the business model — contract API manufacture for individual pharma customers — offers no two-sided dynamic to assess.

Reach is broad across Europe, Japan, LATAM, India and RoW with ~900 customers, but nothing in the calls suggests a service or distribution network rivals cannot replicate; growth is driven by capacity and filings, not reach.
scores.quote: strong execution across markets, including Europe, Japan, Latam, RoW and India

scores.rationale: Sustained growth capex into new engines (Enzene US CDMO plant, biosimilars, MedTech) with capex guided at INR600-700cr in FY25 and INR1,100cr for Occlutech, but incremental ROIC is unproven with a stated ~10-year payback on the largest asset.
scores.quote: It will be to the tune of 600 to 700 crores.

scores.rationale: A&P is discussed almost entirely as a cost line to be controlled (higher marketing/travel expense hurting margins) rather than as brand-equity investment with measurable payback.
scores.quote: mainly it is on account of some additional marketing expenditure

scores.rationale: R&D held consistently at 4-5% of sales across FY24-FY26 and has produced a 7-product biosimilar portfolio, steady ANDA flow and a successful day-1 semaglutide launch that took ~11% unit share.
scores.quote: R&D expenses for the whole year were INR6,173 million, which is 4.2% of the total revenue

scores.rationale: The Occlutech deal is the opposite of a small complementary bolt-on: INR1,100cr for 55% of a cross-border medtech company outside the core, with only ~10% EBITDA expected by FY27, a INR450-500cr debt load and a ~10-year payback.
scores.quote: the payback is around 10 years on this asset

scores.rationale: A coherent, articulated payout policy of 25-30% of PAT with a commitment to hold the absolute dividend through a rising tax rate, though no buyback discipline is evidenced.
scores.quote: currently, I think we actually declare 25 % to 30% of our PAT as dividend

scores.rationale: Mixed evidence: the large trade-generics business is largely outsourced (asset-light), but the company is simultaneously adding owned plants (Enzene US, MedTech manufacturing) and no turnover metrics or moat protection are discussed.
scores.quote: A lot of them is outsourced what we do

scores.rationale: Consistent multi-year share capture from a non-dominant top-5 position — rank gains in antidiabetic and derma in FY23, IPM outperformance in six therapies by FY26, and ~11% unit share within weeks of the semaglutide launch.
scores.quote: we have outperformed IPM in six therapies... derma 1.8x

scores.rationale: International scaled past INR4,000cr in FY24 and grew 22-26% through FY26, with Occlutech adding US/Western Europe/Japan access, though this is generics/devices rather than a premium brand travelling.
scores.quote: International sales were at INR12,157 million with a Y -o-Y growth of 26.6%

scores.rationale: Management explicitly banks growth on volume because ~30% of the portfolio is NLEM price-controlled, offset only partly by a favourable chronic mix that improves roughly 1 percentage point a year.
scores.quote: On this 30% portfolio, it will be largely driven by volumes

scores.rationale: The company sat near the bottom of the US price-erosion cycle in FY23-24 and correctly called the turn, with erosion stabilising at low single digits and US sales subsequently compounding at 20%+.
scores.quote: we are seeing the prices getting more or less bottomed out for many products

scores.rationale: Core end markets are in secular expansion — Indian pharma, the GLP-1 wave, and a $10bn Indian medtech market at $7 per-capita spend versus $50 in China.
scores.quote: India is still an underpenetrated market per capita $7 for India. It's $50 for China.

scores.rationale: Leverage is prudent with a ~INR3,550cr net cash position built from operating cash, but the organic-focus test fails given the largest acquisition in a decade into an unrelated medtech vertical.
scores.quote: Occlutech is one of our biggest investment in last 10 years

scores.rationale: Promises made in FY23 were delivered over four years — chronic/antidiabetic outperformance, the biosimilar 'inflection by 2026', and EBITDA moving from 7.9% in Q1FY23 to 20.4% in FY26 — with management explicitly refusing to reinvent strategy annually.
scores.quote: there is no strategic lever for '26, '27. Every year, we don't have a strategic lever.

scores.rationale: Calls are operationally focused with execution-over-narrative language and no personality-driven promotion, though the company is a widely covered top-5 IPM name.
scores.quote: we'll focus on execution of whatever strategy we have planned out

scores.rationale: Repeated senior churn — two chairmen and two CFOs exiting within FY24, and the CEO departing in FY26 — with new-vertical leadership hired externally rather than promoted from an internal pipeline.
scores.quote: Dr. Vikas is going to now kind of proceed from Alkem

scores.rationale: Management quantifies one-offs, admits guidance misses and owns operational failures such as the trade-generics sales cut-off, though it deflects on specifics like Occlutech promoter stake and cost impacts.
scores.quote: because of the sales cutoff issues, we could not deliver. So, the reporte d growth is on the lower side

scores.rationale: The dramatic FY23-FY26 margin expansion is substantially attributable to external tailwinds — falling API prices and the end of US price erosion — which management itself credits alongside internal cost work, so results overstate demonstrated skill.
scores.quote: on the back of benefits through implementing various cost control initiatives as well as the favorable API prices

scores.rationale: Pioneer-led leadership in trade generics and the number-one anti-infective position create a mind-share franchise, though it is leadership within a fragmented market rather than a true monopoly.
scores.quote: we are the largest trade generic player in the country

scores.rationale: Core branded/trade generics carry no meaningful switching costs for prescribers or stockists; only the newly acquired Occlutech sits behind genuine regulatory entry barriers, and that is unproven for Alkem.
scores.quote: high entry barrier markets, which is -- which include United States and Western Europe

scores.rationale: The Indian pharma and trade-generics markets are fragmented and openly contested, with peers and private-label generics entering the company's franchise and NLEM regulation capping pricing power.
scores.quote: a lot of your peers have no w started to enter into this space

scores.rationale: Low barriers are evident across the portfolio — new trade-generic entrants, structural US price erosion, and government-mandated NLEM pricing that management concedes it cannot mitigate.
scores.quote: the market is competitive, but I think that's a nature of our market

scores.rationale: The company consistently grows 1.2x to 2x the IPM across six therapies, implying a pool of sub-market-growth competitors from which share is being taken.
scores.quote: Vitamins and minerals, we are growing 2x of the market

scores.rationale: Alkem is a top-five IPM company covered by Motilal Oswal, Nomura, BofA, HSBC and Macquarie, and is now expanding into a high-visibility GLP-1 and medtech space — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: The company continues to rank among the top five companies in the Indian pharmaceutical market.

scores.rationale: Genuine brand recall exists in trade generics and branded prescriptions, but gross margin sits around 57-60% and pricing power is capped by NLEM on ~30% of the portfolio.
scores.quote: they do have a very good brand recall with a lot of customers and stockists and retailers

scores.rationale: Reliability/trust is referenced only obliquely (brand image retention at Occlutech, day-1 supply readiness), with no evidence customers pay a premium for certainty over price.
scores.quote: this is a big, big brand which we have bought, and we want to retain the brand ima ge as it

scores.rationale: Accessibility is the company's clearest customer benefit — a large field force driving volume growth, deep stockist intimacy, and active management of channel effectiveness and service levels.
