scores.rationale: Real switching-cost-like protection exists through PGCIL/state utility plant and product approvals and 12-18 month qualification cycles, though the company is one of several qualified suppliers rather than a captive one.
scores.quote: the approval qualification process of the power sector tender takes 12 to 18 months

scores.rationale: The EHV segment has genuinely few qualified players and high entry barriers, but the end customers are state and central PSU utilities buying through competitive tenders, so buyer negotiating power remains strong.
scores.quote: This segment is characterized by high entry barriers, longer customer qualification cycles, and structurally better margins

scores.rationale: Pricing has stayed rational with no discount war and management sees none coming, but this is tested by ~60,000 MVA of new industry capacity from CG Power and Transformers & Rectifiers plus the easing of restrictions on Chinese bidders.
scores.quote: we don't see any impacts on the order inflow, neither do we see any correction on the pricing terms

scores.rationale: Incumbent multinationals have under-invested in India because they find export markets more profitable, and the single Chinese plant in India is fully booked for 18-20 months, leaving demand available to Atlanta.
scores.quote: the market beyond India is more profitable for them... So India has not been a lucrative market for any of these players.

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a hot recent IPO in the most crowded theme in Indian capital goods, with mutual funds and brokers queuing on every call and competitors pouring capital into the same capacity.
scores.quote: Today marks a proud milestone for Atlanta Electricals, our very first quarterly results after listing

scores.rationale: There is no image or taste-based pricing power — gross margin of 27.3% is respectable for the sector but realisation is explicitly tied to commodity prices through pass-through clauses rather than brand.
scores.quote: Revenue per MVA is directly related to the commodity pricing, and commodity pricing is clearly -- naturally hedged to the customer orders itself.

scores.rationale: Customers are buying certainty — PGCIL and state utility approvals, seven NABL-accredited labs, and a 4,700-transformer/1,07,000 MVA delivery record are what win repeat orders like the INR298cr GETCO award.
scores.quote: These orders reflect deep trust built over three decades of partnership with Gujarat's premier state transmission utility.

scores.rationale: Breadth of reach is evident (251 customers across 19 states and three union territories) but no distinctive accessibility, service intimacy or sales-force advantage is described.
scores.quote: Over 200 active customers across 19 states and three union territories

scores.rationale: Customer base is ~70% utility/corporate and the benefit offered matches correctly — reliability, approvals and execution track record rather than consumer intangibles — with approval cycles creating lock-in.
scores.quote: our competitive strength lies in three decades of customer relationship, providing execution track record and expand manufacturing footprint

scores.rationale: Technology is acquired or partnered rather than proprietary — EHV design came via the BTW asset purchase after cancelling the Chinese licence, and 765 kV still awaits a technical-partner agreement; no R&D intensity is disclosed.
scores.quote: The steps we have taken to close the transaction was to first cancel the technology license agreement and then buy the assets

scores.rationale: A tender-based capital goods manufacturer with no two-sided platform dynamic; nothing in five calls suggests value compounds with user scale.

Reach across 19 states and 251 customers is broad and supported by seven in-house testing labs, but sales are won through utility tenders rather than any distribution or service network rivals cannot replicate.
scores.quote: we have added three NABL-accredited testing laboratories during the quarter, taking our total tally to seven

scores.rationale: Sustained growth investment in distribution, branches and technology rather than maintenance, with ROA improving to 1.6-1.8% and ROE ~15%, though incremental returns are good-not-exceptional.
scores.quote: in the last two years, we have nearly doubled our retail asset distribution to about 900 to 1,000 branches for each of our retail secured businesses

scores.rationale: Consistent, deliberate brand investment ('Badlaav Humse Hai') alongside record CASA acquisition growth, but brand equity is still being built rather than proven pricing power.
scores.quote: New CASA account acquisition for FY '26 grew by 62% year -on-year, crossing the milestone of 1 lakh monthly acquisitions

scores.rationale: Bank-equivalent R&D in tech/AI has produced deployable outputs — AI loan origination, scorecards, collections bots, Customer 360 — with measurable efficiency gains, though ROI is still early.
scores.quote: Our first AI -native loan origination system built on this platform went live last week for our gold loan business

scores.rationale: The Fincare deal was a large, transformational merger (not a small bolt-on) that imported an MFI book which promptly drove elevated credit costs, and integration took until April 2026.
scores.quote: MFI, which is 7% of our book is cyclical nature and asset quality is elevated, driven by industry-wide issue of overleveraging

scores.rationale: Distribution is a token ₹1/share dividend with no buybacks; the bank is a net capital raiser (₹2,500 crore QIP) to fund growth, which is coherent but not a shareholder-distribution strength.
scores.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of ■1 per share for FY26

scores.rationale: A bank is structurally balance-sheet heavy — returns come from leverage on a ₹1.58 lakh crore deposit base with ROA only 1.6-1.8%, the opposite of asset-light.
scores.quote: profit after tax increased by 25% year -on-year to ■2,641 crores with ROA of 1.6%

scores.rationale: Loans and deposits are compounding at roughly 1.5-2x the private-sector banking system rate off a small base, i.e. demonstrated share capture with long runway.
scores.quote: Loan portfolio grew by 23% year -on-year versus private sector banking growth of 17%

scores.rationale: Credible domestic expansion beyond the Rajasthan core into South and East India with early contribution emerging, though it is intra-India rather than a brand travelling globally.
scores.quote: increase our productivity in newer geographies like Andhra, Karnataka, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, and UP

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume/balance-sheet led with yields broadly flat; margin gains came from falling cost of funds and seasonality, not pricing power.
scores.quote: Our yield on assets -- yield on gross advances was broadly stable at 14.4%

scores.rationale: The MFI/unsecured credit cycle bottomed in FY25 and the bank is now on the visible upturn with credit costs nearly halving year-on-year.
scores.quote: Credit cost, including CGFMU fee, declined by 54 basis points year -on-year to 0.8% compared with 1.4% a year ago

scores.rationale: Retail and small-business credit penetration in India is in secular expansion, and management explicitly anchors growth at a multiple of nominal GDP.
scores.quote: capable of sustainably compounding at 2 to 2.5 x of India's nominal GDP growth rate

scores.rationale: Largely organic, conservative underwriting and willingness to shrink unsecured books when risk rose, offset by the sizeable Fincare acquisition and repeated equity raises.
scores.quote: we have taken a very kind of call where we just want to understand more digital credit

scores.rationale: Founder-led for a decade with a consistently articulated multi-year 'forever bank' horizon and explicit rejection of quarter-to-quarter management, backed by RBI extension of tenure to 2029.
scores.quote: We are not working with a quarter -to-quarter mentality , instead focusing on the long term horizon

scores.rationale: Management is accessible and hosts investor 'AU Insights' sessions with a visible founder persona, but commentary stays operational rather than celebrity-driven — a neutral read.
scores.quote: our third AU Insights session is scheduled for the 3rd of November

scores.rationale: Deep and demonstrated internal pipeline — CFO, Deputy CEO and Executive Director roles all filled by internal elevations, with an explicit SBU-based succession structure.
scores.quote: Mr. Yogesh Jain has been elevated as the Deputy CEO of the bank

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly disclosed missed guidance and problem areas unprompted, including admitting credit cost exceeded its own promise and that credit cards are loss-making.
scores.quote: we don't want to overcommit ourselves that our credit cost can be in the range of 1.15 - 1.20% as we promised

scores.rationale: Recent 65% profit growth is substantially cycle-normalisation and falling cost of funds rather than pure skill, so results should be discounted toward a ~1.6% ROA / 14% ROE steady state.
scores.quote: Provisions were down 19% quarter -on-quarter on account of normalization in unsecured businesses

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position in the customer's mind; the bank competes for both assets and deposits and is a price-taker in its largest product.
scores.quote: grew by 11% year -on-year to approximately ■42,400 crores in a highly competitive market

scores.rationale: Modest switching-cost build via CASA primacy, cross-sell and commercial-banking transaction stickiness, but nothing approaching a captive or regional monopoly.
scores.quote: our intent is to progressively run this as a fully self-funded business, a model that strengthens both margin resilience and customer stickiness

scores.rationale: Indian banking is a fragmented, highly competitive market where AU is a small player facing intense deposit competition, not a stable oligopoly.
scores.quote: Liquidity conditions remain r elatively tight with heightened competition for deposits

scores.rationale: RBI licensing is a genuine entry barrier, but pricing discipline in the industry is imperfect, with competitive rate-setting on both deposits and mortgages.
scores.quote: the rationale behind hiking interest rate in savings account and TD much ahead of the industry

scores.rationale: Weakened NBFCs/MFIs and slower-growing incumbents are ceding ground, evidenced by AU growing deposits at 24% against 14% for the private-bank system.
scores.quote: Deposits growth remained robust at 24% year -on-year, significantly ahead of the estimated private sector banking deposit growth of 14%

scores.rationale: A heavily analyst-covered listed bank actively courting a universal banking licence and brand visibility is the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: upgrade to Universal Bank license will strengthen our deposit franchise with a better brand acceptance

scores.rationale: High headline NIM of ~5.9% reflects risk-segment pricing in informal self-employed lending rather than image-driven pricing power; brand is still being built.
scores.quote: Around 80% of our book is in this informal self-employed customer segments

scores.rationale: Depositors buy safety and trust, and management explicitly frames the universal licence as raising perceived safety, though AU still pays above-market rates to attract funds.
scores.quote: higher customer perception of safety and trust

scores.rationale: Dense physical touch points combined with a dominant digital channel and a large feet-on-street force give genuine accessibility and customer intimacy in underserved geographies.
scores.quote: more than 90% of the bank's transactions and service requests now being processed through AU 0101

scores.rationale: Benefit types are reasonably matched — convenience and cross-sell for retail/informal borrowers, and transaction-banking/CMS lock-in for commercial customers.
scores.quote: increased penetration of transaction banking, CMS, trade, and other relationship -led offerings

scores.rationale: Serious and broad AI/data investment, but built largely on third-party platforms (Salesforce, Darwinbox) that larger banks can match or exceed, so no durable tech edge yet.
scores.quote: our wheels business runs entirely on Salesforce LOS, personal loans are now live on the same platform

scores.rationale: No two-sided network is described anywhere across the calls; growth comes from distribution and cross-sell, and scale does not make the product better for other users.
Distribution reach is the core moat — 2,400+ touch points scaled to ~900-1,300 branches per product line, extended further via Fincare, in semi-urban markets larger banks underserve.
scores.quote: taking total gold loan distributions to over 1,300 branches

scores.rationale: Growth capex and capitalised development have scaled sharply (intangibles from ~₹20-30cr to ~₹200cr) into data centres, transit and AI, but incremental returns are unproven — FY26 PAT grew only 9% for 9M and cash flows were negative mid-year.
scores.quote: going from like INR 20 crores to INR 30 crores to INR 200 crores

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend across the calls; the business sells via enterprise tenders and partnerships.

R&D held at 9-10% of revenue for years and has consistently converted into products and wins — Chartis leaders-quadrant IP, Omnifin, Arya.AI, AurionAi, Orion-MSP and an AI-native trade finance platform.
scores.quote: R&D spending, we expect that to remain in the range of 9% to 10% of revenues

scores.rationale: A steady stream of small complementary bolt-ons (ATAS, SC Soft, AS Software/Omnifin, Arya.AI) that filled genuine product gaps, but post-deal OPM has not improved (EBITDA margin drifting from 22% to 20%) and earlier acquisitions like cybersecurity and smart city were divested or shrunk.
scores.quote: AS, which was the Omnifin product that we acquired, that is clearly was a gap in our strategic blueprint for the lending space

scores.rationale: No buyback or dividend policy is discussed in any excerpt; capital flow has been the other way via the FY25 QIP.

The model has become progressively asset- and working-capital-heavy — hardware manufacturing, platform screen doors, data-centre builds, ~₹200cr of intangibles, DSOs of 100-110 days and negative H1 operating cash flow.
scores.quote: DSOs, what I have said in the past, something between 100 and 110

scores.rationale: A small player in very large markets with clear evidence of capture — 23 new logos in one quarter, landmark Singapore bank lending mandate, iCash pro becoming the standard for new deals, and entry into IDBI.
scores.quote: We added 23 new logos across our business segments, one of the fastest rates of customer additions in our journey

scores.rationale: Genuine multi-year international build-out (California, LatAm, Africa, UK, Australia, Middle East) has driven growth, but FY26 exposed concentration risk when the MEA war cost committed closures and Europe is still 'maturing slowly'.
scores.quote: The Middle East has become an increasingly important growth engine over the last couple of years... and we fell really short there

scores.rationale: Growth is volume/order-led rather than price- or mix-led — management explicitly declines margin expansion and mix is shifting toward hardware and data-centre work, with EBITDA margin drifting from 22% (FY23) to ~20% (FY26).
scores.quote: the game plan is for the next two, three years to not focus on margin expansion

scores.rationale: The only cyclical framing is a temporary MEA geopolitical trough expected to recover, while the core end markets (AI data centres, transit capex) are already in an up-cycle rather than near a bottom.
scores.quote: The spend appetite in the region is intact once the geopolitical picture clears

scores.rationale: All three engines — enterprise AI for banks, Indian data-centre capacity for AI compute, and metro/transit fare systems — are in structural secular expansion with TAMs management says have grown manifold.
scores.quote: we had no idea of the scale of demand that will come from, for example, AI compute

scores.rationale: Counter-cyclical, conviction-led investment and no large M&A are offset by continuous small acquisitions, equity dilution via QIP, rising working-capital borrowing and self-acknowledged balance-sheet strain.
scores.quote: We would rather absorb temporary balance sheet pressure than underinvest when the opportunity is this clear

scores.rationale: A single strategic thesis set out in 2022 (IP-led products in banking, transit, data centres) has been pursued through Vision 2030 with ~32-33% five-year CAGR and the business quadrupling, including willingness to sacrifice near-term margin for the AI rebuild.
scores.quote: over the last five years, we are proud that CAGR is at 32%, 33%

scores.rationale: The CEO's commentary is consistently promotional and superlative-heavy rather than understated, with repeated claims of category leadership and self-comparison against peers.
scores.quote: I do not know of any firm which navigated it better than we did

scores.rationale: Team quality is praised and the CFO/CS have been stable through the period, but there is no described succession or talent-development system, and management admits the organisation is stretched while deliberately decoupling headcount from revenue.
scores.quote: five years of this space has left us stretched in places

scores.rationale: Management openly owns the FY26 miss, calls its own result below par, accepts responsibility rather than blaming only geopolitics, and had similarly disclosed working-capital and execution delays back in 2022.
scores.quote: By our own standards, the final result was below par. We can do better and we will.

scores.rationale: Stripping the narrative from the numbers shows repeated guidance slippage (30-35% guided vs 20.2% delivered in FY26), 9M PAT up only 9%, margin compression and negative interim cash flows, so results lag the rhetoric.
scores.quote: we planned for the revenue to grow close to 30%. In reality, the revenue actually grew 20.2%

scores.rationale: Some products approach mind-share monopoly in their niche — iCash pro is described as setting the market standard for new transaction-banking deals and the company was the only Asian vendor in three Chartis leaders quadrants — but this is niche-level rather than company-wide.
scores.quote: That pretty much sets up iCash pro as the market standard pretty much for most of the new deals

scores.rationale: Very high switching costs in regulated core banking with effectively perpetual maintenance annuities, plus captive installed-base positions in metro fare-collection systems.
scores.quote: we rarely lose a customer once they start using Aurionpro software... Changing software is a very painful task

scores.rationale: Core markets are contested global tenders against many international players, and the customers are large banks, metros and government bodies with strong procurement power, not a stable oligopoly.
scores.quote: our win in the highly competitive global tender for state of California, competing with leading players across the world

scores.rationale: Deep IP and regulatory certification create real barriers in banking and transit, but the spaces are bid-based and the AI shift is drawing in new capital and potential frontier-model entrants that management is explicitly asked about.
scores.quote: is there any competition from platforms like Anthropic and OpenAI to your present suite?

scores.rationale: The explicit strategy is taking share from slower legacy core-banking vendors, with the AI-native stack positioned as the displacement wedge.
scores.quote: we have like an opportunity to displace the legacy vendors at large scale across the globe

scores.rationale: The company is no longer under the radar — a QIP drew prominent global and Indian institutions, it runs regular IR events, and it operates in the two most capital-attracting themes (AI and data centres).
scores.quote: we concluded a successful QIP and it's very encouraging to attract prominent global and Indian institutions

scores.rationale: There is no image- or taste-driven pricing power; EBITDA sits at ~20% against management's own view that software businesses should earn 40-50%, with hardware and systems content diluting the mix.
scores.quote: software businesses are capable of driving, 40%, 45%, 50% EBITDA... this is not the time to do it

scores.rationale: Customers are buying mission-critical certainty — regulated banks running core lending and transaction banking, RBI tier-four data centre design, and safety-critical platform screen doors — where trust and references outweigh price.
scores.quote: serious banks, serious insurers are using our mission critical applications to run their businesses

scores.rationale: Distribution reach and customer intimacy have improved materially via expanded sales channels and tie-ups with Mastercard, Vix and hyperscalers, feeding a record logo-addition quarter, though management still frames distribution as the binding constraint.
scores.quote: our expanding sales channel and the strategic partnerships that we forged with the large global technology players

scores.rationale: The customer base is almost entirely corporate and government, and the value proposition is correctly matched to it — reliability, single-window delivery and long-lived switching-cost lock-in rather than brand intangibles.
scores.quote: strengthening our position as the go-to solution provider, as a single-window data center solutions provider

scores.rationale: Deep multi-product IP with sustained 9-10% R&D intensity, externally validated (only Asian vendor in three Chartis leaders quadrants), and now proprietary research producing a top-ranked tabular foundation model and an agentic trade-finance stack.
scores.quote: We are the No. 1 or No. 2 foundation model for tabular data in the world on most of the global benchmarks

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is described anywhere in the calls; growth comes from tenders, partnerships and product wins.

Global reach and delivery capability have been built out over five years, but management repeatedly frames distribution as the limiting factor to be expanded rather than an advantage rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: the idea is let's capitalize on the demand by expanding distribution

scores.rationale: Sustained heavy growth capex ($61m/qtr in FY23 rising to $341m in FY26) across Pen-G, China OSD, Vizag injectables, Dayton/Raleigh and a biologics CMO, but incremental returns have lagged badly — Pen-G and China ran ~₹200cr+ EBITDA losses in FY26 and CMO revenue only starts 2028.
scores.quote: Net CapEx for the quarter is $82 million and for the year around $341 million, which includes capacity enhancement projects and plant expenses and CMO project.

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any excerpt.

R&D held steadily at 4.5–5% of revenue (₹310cr in Q1FY23 to ₹1,590cr in FY26) and consistently converts into filings and launches (838 cumulative ANDAs, 9 launches/7 approvals in Q3FY26) plus a biosimilar pipeline extending to 2032, though generic R&D yields commoditised products with ongoing price erosion.
scores.quote: R&D expenditure was Rs. 409 crores, amounting to 5% of the total revenues, thereby reinforcing our commitment on continue to build a robust pipeline

scores.rationale: Deals are mostly complementary bolt-ons (Khandelwal non-oncology ~$32m, domestic pharma portfolio $251m, Indonesia) and management disavows big-bang M&A, but Lannett is a ~$300m distressed US generic asset — not an already-strong acquiree — and post-deal OPM benefit is unproven.
scores.quote: We are not going for any big bang acquisition, at least I hope we don't.

scores.rationale: First-ever ₹750cr buyback completed Aug-2024 at ₹1,460 with an explicit tax-efficiency rationale alongside a ₹264cr dividend, showing an emerging but still short and thin distribution policy.
scores.quote: we will be completing our first ever buyback of Rs. 750 crores in August '24 at a price of Rs. 1,460... will provide tax efficient return to our shareholders

scores.rationale: The business is structurally asset-heavy — six plants under commissioning in FY23, depreciation above ₹400cr/quarter, and continuous $70–80m quarterly capex on capacity that takes years to generate revenue — with no moat protecting the deployed assets.
scores.quote: as on date, there are six plants are under commissioning

scores.rationale: Repeated evidence of share capture — US volume gains and market share gains, and European growth of low-double-digit to 27% against a market growing 0–3% — in fragmented markets where Aurobindo is far from dominant.
scores.quote: Low double digit in itself is well ahead of the market growth rate.

scores.rationale: Well-executed multi-geography build-out: Europe hit its promised €1bn FY26 milestone, growth markets grew 25% y/y with Canada expansion, China OSD is scaling toward 2bn units and India is being built as a new engine — though it is generic supply, not a premium brand that travels.
scores.quote: For the full year, European formulations achieved a significant milestone of €1 billion revenue

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly volume-led with pricing at best neutral and often eroding (3% erosion in FY23, 'pricing pressures' still cited in FY26), the opposite of price/mix-led growth.
scores.quote: The growth was mainly driven by volume gains, stable demand and new product launches, while on an overall basis, price erosion remained neutral.

scores.rationale: The company moved off a clear cyclical trough — Q1FY23 EBITDA margin of 15.5% amid freight/raw-material inflation and price erosion recovered to 20.4% for FY26 on benign input costs — and a fresh catalyst (the Pen-G minimum import price notification) sits ahead, though the easy part of the upcycle is now behind.
scores.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter was 15.5%

scores.rationale: End markets are in secular expansion — generics volume demand, complex generics across dermal/transdermal/nasal/respiratory/oncology, biosimilars to 2032, GLP-1 cartridge lines and a biologics CMO — supporting durable long-run demand.
scores.quote: increasing focus on complex generics across dermal, transdermal, nasal, respiratory and oncology

scores.rationale: Consistently prudent balance sheet across the period — gross debt cut from $313m to $277m in FY23, net cash of $317m by Mar-26 — with counter-cyclical capex through the downcycle and a stated aversion to big-bang M&A, tempered by an accelerating acquisition cadence (Lannett, Khandelwal, portfolio deals).
scores.quote: we reduced the gross debt significantly to $277 million from $313 million end March '22

scores.rationale: Multi-year projects promised in 2022 were seen through despite repeated setbacks — Pen-G went from 'teething problems' in FY25 to >10,000 MT annualised at >80% utilisation and positive EBITDA by FY26, and biosimilars were pushed through years of trials to EMA/FDA filings.
scores.quote: we expect to produce more than 10,000 metric tonnes on annualised basis over the next 12 months. It is important to note that the yield levels are steady and improving consistently

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently substance-first, run by the CFO and business-unit CEOs with operational detail and no promotional or celebrity framing, and the chairman deflected rather than talked up the share price question.
scores.quote: while we may not like to comment on the movement of the share price

scores.rationale: A real bench of business-unit CEOs has been built out (Eugia, US, Europe, biosimilars) and IR/leadership roles have rotated, but the group CEO succession answer in 2022 was to defer for 'two to three years' with promoter family retaining control, showing an incomplete pipeline at the top.
scores.quote: I don't think we are looking but, we are going to appoint in next two to three years.

scores.rationale: Management discloses negatives specifically and unprompted — a >₹100cr remediation/production-delay hit, ₹200cr+ Pen-G/6-APA EBITDA loss, the prior data-integrity findings, and refusing to raise guidance until it could be substantiated — rather than glossing.
scores.quote: we do not have any data integrity issues, which was the issue last time unfortunately

scores.rationale: Much of the FY24–FY26 profit improvement traces to factors outside management skill — gRevlimid one-off exclusivity sales, gross margin lifted from 53.9% to 59.4% by benign raw material prices, and a government minimum-import-price notification on Pen-G — so results overstate underlying operating skill.
scores.quote: The Government of India issued a notification introducing a one-year CIF on minimum import price for Pen-G, 6 APA and Amoxicillin. The policy change will act as a very important and positive catalyst

scores.rationale: Nothing in the evidence suggests a monopoly-like position in customers' minds — it is an interchangeable generic supplier facing continuous price erosion and competing on volume and service levels.
scores.quote: the price erosion for example, this quarter, compared to the previous quarter is about 2% plus

scores.rationale: No captive aftermarket or switching costs; generic substitution means customers can swap suppliers freely, which is why sales are defended by portfolio breadth rather than lock-in.
scores.quote: Our large product portfolio helps us to maintain optimally the price stability.

scores.rationale: US generics is the opposite of a stable oligopoly — persistent multi-year price erosion and shelf-stock adjustments show consolidated buyers hold the negotiating power over many interchangeable suppliers.
scores.quote: including the shelf stock adjustment, it's closer to around 3%

scores.rationale: Pricing has been chronically irrational with erosion in US orals and injectables throughout the period, though rising barriers in complex injectables, biosimilars and Pen-G backward integration partly offset this.
scores.quote: Ex-gRevlimid, growth was 12%, mainly due to improved supplies, new product launches partly offset by pricing pressures.

scores.rationale: Weak competitors are visibly donating share — Aurobindo is acquiring distressed US generic player Lannett, taking base business from rivals, and winning European share on reliable supply while others struggle.
scores.quote: we also tried to get some of the base business additionally. So, we have been partly successful in that.

scores.rationale: This is a widely-covered large-cap with a crowded analyst roster (HSBC and multiple brokerages on every call) and a retail shareholder base actively debating the share price — not an ignored niche.
scores.quote: I would like to ask the question on behalf of the retail investors.

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power: gross margin near 60% comes from input-cost softening and mix rather than brand, and the company is a price-taker facing erosion.
scores.quote: Gross margin for that quarter stood at 59.7%, supported by softer raw material prices and business mix.

scores.rationale: Reliability is genuinely a selling point in Europe where supply capability drives customer partnerships, but repeated FDA setbacks — an OAI, a still-unlifted warning letter at Eugia and prior data-integrity findings — undercut the assurance proposition.
scores.quote: we are yet to get full clearance from the FDA... So, it should be in that same trajectory till the time the warning letter gets lifted.

scores.rationale: There is expanding access — deeper pan-India reach via new divisions and acquisitions, new geographies in growth markets — but no evidence of customer intimacy or sales-force strength as a differentiator.
scores.quote: continues to expand through new divisions, wider therapeutic presence and deeper pan-India reach

scores.rationale: The customer base is corporate (US distributors, tenders, European buyers) where the required lock-in via switching costs is absent — the relationship rests on price and supply, evidenced by ARV tender-driven sales and constant price erosion.
scores.quote: The continued growth momentum was driven by higher volumes and new tender wins

scores.rationale: Genuine multi-product technical depth is being built — biosimilars filed with EMA/FDA, peptides/GLP-1 cartridge lines, complex generics and rare Pen-G/6-APA fermentation backward integration — at ~5% R&D intensity, though it is not yet delivering superior customer-visible benefit.
scores.quote: we have a cartridge line where like we will be taking all the GLP-1 products from there and we'll be filing

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network exists in this manufacturing-and-supply model; scale benefits described are operating leverage, not network effects.
scores.quote: With manufacturing capacity exceeding 60 billion units and further expansion underway, we are well-positioned to support rising demand

scores.rationale: Distribution and supply reach is a real scale advantage — 60bn+ unit capacity feeding US, all key European geographies, growth markets and India, with reliable supply explicitly cited as what wins European customers, in a category where service levels matter.
scores.quote: Our operational execution, expanding product basket and reliable supply capability continued to drive our performance and reinforce customer partnership.

scores.rationale: Capex is deliberately modest (~INR56 cr in FY26, ~INR50 cr/yr guided) but is genuinely growth-directed — two new Chennai plants and a brownfield Phase 1/2 — and converts into 46% revenue growth with ROCE rising from ~10% to 20.6%, though the absolute growth capex is not 'high and rising'.
scores.quote: We continue to follow a capex -light model... Asset turns are at 9.9 times, and return on capital employed improved to 20.6% from 15.7% a year ago

scores.rationale: No advertising or promotion spend is discussed anywhere across the calls — it is a B2B contract manufacturer with no consumer brand.

No R&D line item is disclosed, but the in-house design/NPD engine (India's largest PCB design team, prototype-to-production pipeline) has repeatedly converted into named new programs — semiconductor equipment, satellite antenna control units, aerospace cabin subassemblies — with FY27 revenue visibility.
scores.quote: We have successfully completed the first tranche of prototypes for a communication customer where we are manufacturing control units for satellite antenna systems. We expect volume orders to commence from FY '27.

scores.rationale: No acquisitions are mentioned in any of the three years of excerpts; the company has grown purely organically, so there is no M&A track record to judge.
No dividend, buyback or distribution policy is discussed; the only capital-return-adjacent action is IPO-proceeds debt repayment, which is not a shareholder distribution.

Asset turn has stayed structurally high across the whole period (10.4x in FY23, 7.5x at the FY25 trough, 9.9x in FY26) on a capex-light model with net debt/equity of 0.06 and ROCE of 20.6%, and the moat element is supported by long-life mission-critical box-build programs.
scores.quote: We have always maintained that we'll do asset turns between 7 to 10x and we'll continue to do so.

scores.rationale: Avalon is a small player in a fragmented, fast-expanding market with large runway (India EMS share targeted to move 2.2%→7%) and it is demonstrably capturing share, growing 46% in FY26 versus far slower industry growth, with box build rising 44%→56%.
scores.quote: India is eyeing a market share growth from 2.2% to 7%

scores.rationale: The dual-shore India/US model is executed and now a stated selling point, with new expansion into Southeast Asia and a Europe sales presence, but the US manufacturing arm has been loss-making for years and only targets breakeven in late FY27, so execution is credible rather than clean.
scores.quote: we have made progress in expanding exports to Southeast Asia, further broadening our geographic footprint

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume/new-program led — gross margin has been range-bound at 33–35% throughout while revenue grew 46% — with the only pricing-adjacent evidence being tariff pass-through and a favourable box-build mix shift, not price realisation.
scores.quote: Gross margin for the year was 34.3% at the upper end of our guided range... revenue was at INR1,603 crores, up 46% year -on-year

scores.rationale: Management correctly identified the US destocking trough in Aug 2024 and the predicted upturn delivered seven straight quarters of growth, but the stock of that cyclical recovery is now largely harvested, so the company sits well past the bottom rather than near it.
scores.quote: we believe we have reached the bottom and are now seeing strong signs of recovery in the second half of this year

scores.rationale: End markets are in secular expansion on multiple independent legs — India EMS inflection/China+1, ISM 2.0 semiconductor equipment, clean energy storage, rail Kavach, aerospace — each of which produced actual order wins, not just narrative.
scores.quote: the government direction towards India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 with a focus on semiconductor equipment aligns well with our capabilities and recent business wins

scores.rationale: Purely organic growth, no acquisitions, net debt/equity of 0.06, capex-light discipline maintained through the FY25 downturn, and an explicit refusal to chase subsidised greenfield component manufacturing that peers are pursuing.
scores.quote: instead of trying to do a greenfield, though there's a lot of money available for that... we like to stay focused and deliver on what we say

scores.rationale: Management articulated a long-horizon thesis in 2023, held to it through a loss-making FY25 quarter, and delivered the FY24→FY27 doubling a full year early, with aerospace wins explicitly the fruit of 8–10 years of patient positioning.
scores.quote: we have previously committed to doubling revenues from FY24 to FY27, a target of approximately INR1,725 crores. We are almost there, a year ahead.

scores.rationale: The team stopped naming marquee customers on calls, guides conservatively and declines quarterly guidance, though the tone in FY26 has become noticeably more promotional ('best year', 'highest ever').
scores.quote: We stopped mentioning names in the calls.

scores.rationale: The leadership bench was systematically deepened (Group COO, Group CSO added in FY25) and the CFO role was filled by internal promotion of Suresh V.R. from Head of Corporate Planning/IR, though the prior CFO's exit and reliance on hiring for future programs temper this.
scores.quote: we'll have to focus on basically people -based investments to get the right person on board

scores.rationale: Management pre-announced the US destocking downturn before it hit, disclosed the US loss in exact rupee terms during the worst quarter, and volunteered that FY26 gross margin percentage was optically flattered/hurt by ~110bps of tariff gross-up rather than letting the number stand.
scores.quote: our US manufacturing business reported a net loss of INR14.2 crores

scores.rationale: Stripping out skill from luck, a material part of the FY26 surge is exogenous — restocking after destocking, a 50%→18% tariff cut, ISM 2.0 and China+1 — and the same team posted a PAT loss in Q1 FY25, so the record does not yet cleanly isolate managerial skill.
scores.quote: U.S. tariffs have reduced from 50% to 18%, benefiting our U.S. export business

scores.rationale: Long, sticky mission-critical programs create real account-level entrenchment, but Avalon holds no monopoly-like position in a customer's mind or in aftermarket/services — it is one qualified supplier among several in a crowded EMS field.
scores.quote: once it comes into production, it normally stays and these are larger Fortune 100 type companies

scores.rationale: Genuine switching costs exist via qualification, NADCAP approvals and deep box-build integration, evidenced by 8–10 year customer lives and the ability to pass through 99% of tariffs, but there is no regional monopoly or captive aftermarket.
scores.quote: we were able to recover 99% of the applicable tariffs from our customers

scores.rationale: Indian EMS is a fragmented, rapidly crowding industry — peers are simultaneously adding components and PCB capacity under ECMS — and the end customers are Fortune 100 buyers with substantial negotiating power, the opposite of a stable oligopoly.
scores.quote: a number of your peers are getting into components manufacturing, like PCB manufacturing and have gotten ECMS scheme for that

scores.rationale: Avalon prices rationally and refuses low-margin volume work, holding 33–35% gross margin through the cycle, but capital is flooding into Indian EMS with new entrants and subsidy schemes, so entry barriers at the industry level are weakening.
scores.quote: We maintain industry -leading gross margins and have not pursued low -margin businesses.

scores.rationale: Share is being donated by higher-cost or China-exposed incumbents as customers actively diversify supply chains, a shift Avalon converted into new program wins during the tariff period.
scores.quote: we accelerated new program wins in the U.S. for U.S. manufacturing, as customers look to diversify supply chains and reduce risk

scores.rationale: The high-mix, flexible-volume complex niche is one large volume players avoid, but the company is a listed, heavily covered name (JM, Motilal Oswal, Macquarie, Kotak, DAM on the calls) in the most fashionable sector in Indian capital markets.
scores.quote: We operate today by choice in high complex, high margin B2B space and not in the low margin, high volume segments.

scores.rationale: Gross margin is high and stable at 33–35% and management calls it industry-leading, but this comes from complexity and mix in a B2B setting, not from image or taste-driven pricing power, which is not applicable here.
scores.quote: on a full -year basis, our gross margins can be between 33% and 35%

scores.rationale: The entire proposition is certainty — mission-critical railway signalling, aerospace, medical, NADCAP-approved fabrication — and customers demonstrated that price is secondary by absorbing 99% of a tariff shock rather than switching suppliers.
scores.quote: we make complex multi -layer assemblies that are used for mission critical applications like railway signalling systems

scores.rationale: Vertical integration into a genuine one-stop box-build plus the dual-shore model lets customers start in the US and migrate to India, which is real accessibility and intimacy, though it depends on a still loss-making US footprint.
scores.quote: Our presence in both India and U.S. gives customers the option to start in the U.S. and later transition to India

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate and the benefits offered are correctly matched — reliability, dual-shore TCO/tariff optimisation and qualification-based lock-in producing 8–10 year product lives rather than intangible appeals.
scores.quote: the average life cycle of a customer with us is very long and product life cycle is also long... they continue for over a period of 8 to 10 years

scores.rationale: The multi-commodity vertical stack (PCB design and assembly, magnetics, sheet metal, plastics, cables, test) is a real and widening capability edge now reaching Industry 4.0 semiconductor equipment, but Avalon builds to customers' designs and discloses no R&D intensity.
scores.quote: We are progressing steadily in this space, partnering with global major to deliver Industry 4.0 compliant complex systems.

scores.rationale: Nothing in the calls describes a two-sided or self-reinforcing network; the business is bilateral contract manufacturing.

A 13–14 plant India-plus-US manufacturing and logistics footprint with local US service support is hard for pure-India peers to match and is actively used to win customers, though it is a manufacturing-proximity advantage rather than a dominant service network.
scores.quote: this is something, which we need for our future as well as the confidence from customers on having local support

scores.rationale: Consistent, self-funded growth capex delivered on schedule across the period — a 1.75 lakh MT feed plant, new pre-processing/cold storage, the Krishnapuram processing plant commissioned March 2024, and now a pet-food facility — though returns are diluted by commodity-linked feed economics.
scores.quote: setting up of new shrimp feed manufacturing facilities in Varadapuram with annual installed capacity of 1,75,000 MT with a CAPEX of Rs. 125 crores

scores.rationale: A&P is essentially absent for the core feed/export business and confined to small digital campaigns for the new pet-care brand, whose sales remain trivial (INR 1.51 crore in Q4 FY26), so no evidence yet of durable brand equity being built.
scores.quote: strengthening the AvantFurst brand through the targeted digital marketing initiatives on Instagram and Facebook

scores.rationale: New product initiatives exist (value-added shrimp up 142%, fish-feed trials) but core technology is licensed in rather than developed — pet food formulations come from Bluefalo Thailand — so R&D efficiency is unproven.
scores.quote: The required technical now, how is being provided by Bluefalo Pet Care Company Limited Thailand

scores.rationale: No acquisitions in five years; diversification is via an organic SPV plus a technology JV, which avoids M&A risk but gives no track record of value-accretive bolt-ons to score positively.
scores.quote: diversified into pet care products business through its subsidiary, Avanti Pet Care Private Limited, as a special purpose vehicle

scores.rationale: The excerpts contain no discussion of dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy.

Asset-light economics — INR 6,279 crore consolidated FY26 revenue off modest plants (a 1.75 lakh MT feed plant cost only INR 125 crore) — but the moat protecting that turn is thin given raw-material and price-control exposure.
scores.quote: The gross income in FY26 is INR 6,279 crores as compared to INR 5,766 crores in FY25

scores.rationale: Already the dominant feed player at roughly half the market with little runway, and volumes have been broadly flat for four years (5.41 lakh MT FY22 to 5.62 lakh MT FY26) against a growing industry pool, implying share erosion rather than capture.
scores.quote: The company is expected to maintain its market share to 48% - 50%

scores.rationale: Credible export diversification away from the US as tariffs bit — exports grew 20% to 16,976 MT in FY26 with new pushes into Japan, Korea, China and the EU.
scores.quote: the company continues to strengthen its presence in other international markets, thereby reducing its dependence on any single geography

scores.rationale: Feed growth is volume- and cost-pass-through-driven with pricing constrained by state government approval, and FY26 feed revenue actually fell on lower sale price despite higher volumes; only the frozen division shows genuine mix/realisation gains.
scores.quote: the recent price rise of Rs. 2.56 paisa had to be rollback by the Government of Andhra Pradesh

scores.rationale: The company is coming off a peak year (FY26 PBT INR 882 crore, +20%) into an explicitly challenging FY27 as fish meal doubled to INR 240/kg, so it sits nearer a cyclical top than a bottom.
scores.quote: FY2627 is expected to be a challenging season for the aquaculture industry in respect of shrimp production due to steep increase in feed raw material prices

scores.rationale: Indian shrimp feed consumption rose from 10.5 lakh MT (FY21) to an estimated 11-12 lakh MT, seafood exports hit an all-time high, and policy support (PMMSY) reinforces the secular trend, though growth is punctuated by disease and climate shocks.
scores.quote: India's seafood exports reached an all-time high of USD 8.546 billion in FY2526

scores.rationale: Five years of organic, debt-light, incremental capacity building with no large acquisitions and diversification funded internally through a small SPV.
scores.quote: the company has purchased the land near Hyderabad... For setting up a state of art manufacturing facility

scores.rationale: Core-business promises were largely delivered (Krishnapuram plant commissioned, USFDA recall terminated and claims settled to nil), but the pet-food diversification promised for launch within '6 to 8 months' in mid-2024 still has no factory under construction two years later.
scores.quote: It is anticipated that this process would take about 6 to 8 months before the launch of the products in India.

scores.rationale: Calls are run by the JMD/CFO with divisional finance heads presenting numbers, consistently substance-heavy and free of promotional or personality-driven commentary across all 17 calls.
scores.quote: I would like to share with you some of the key indicators relevant for our discussion today

scores.rationale: There is visible internal progression (Santhi Latha from GM-Finance to CFO) and dedicated CFOs for each subsidiary, but leadership succession is family-based with no articulated talent-development system.
scores.quote: Mrs. Santhi Latha, Chief Financial Officer, Avanti Feeds Ltd.

scores.rationale: Consistently candid over four years — full provision tables for the salmonella recall, unflinching disclosure of missed feed-sale targets, explicit guidance cuts, and pre-warning of margin pressure before it appears in results.
scores.quote: Considering the continued steep increase in prices of major raw material like fish meal and soya bean meal during the past three months... the PBT for the FY26 is expected to be around 14.5% to 15%

scores.rationale: Strong FY26 results are largely explained by exogenous factors management itself names — falling raw-material prices, favourable FX, lower ocean freight and tariff reversal — so the record does not cleanly evidence managerial skill.
scores.quote: which has direct impact on the raw material cost of the feed, which is beyond the company's control

scores.rationale: A ~48-50% share of Indian shrimp feed gives a leader's position in the farmer's mind, though it is a share-of-commodity leadership rather than an unassailable aftermarket lock.
scores.quote: The company is expected to maintain its market share to 48% - 50%

scores.rationale: Farmers face negligible switching costs and imported feed at 'highly reduced prices' was competitive enough that the industry had to lobby for a 15% duty to stay in the game.
scores.quote: the imported feed was available, highly reduced prices, making a big competition for the domestic feed manufacturers

scores.rationale: Shrimp feed is a concentrated few-player industry with fragmented smallholder farmers on the other side, though pricing power is capped by state-government approval rather than by customers.
scores.quote: We have discussed this with the manufacturers stressing the government; you may recall that the recent price rise of Rs. 2.56 paisa had to be rollback

scores.rationale: Capital and approval requirements deter casual entry and domestic pricing is orderly, but the industry depends on tariff protection against imports and on government price clearance, indicating imperfect structural insulation.
scores.quote: The customs duty on imported shrimp feed has been reinstated at 15%, but withdrawing concession duty at 5%

scores.rationale: Weaker domestic feed players exist below the leaders, but volumes flat at ~5.5 lakh MT across four years show no actual share being harvested from them.
scores.quote: The company feed sales during FY26 is 5,62,060 MT against 5,55,247 MT in FY25

scores.rationale: Aquaculture feed is an unglamorous niche, but Avanti is a widely covered listed leader with institutional analysts (InCred, Kotak, Equirus) on every call, so it is not under the radar of capital.
scores.quote: Nitin Awasthi : InCred Capital / Arjun Khanna : Kotak Mutual Funds / Ronak Shah : Equirus Securities

scores.rationale: There is no image-based pricing power — feed prices need government permission, margins swing entirely with fish meal and soya, and management concedes gross margin is a function of raw material cost.
scores.quote: the EBITDA gross margins depend on the raw material cost for this industry

scores.rationale: Farmers buy feed on reliability of crop outcome and the company positions itself around compliance and food safety, tightening controls after the USFDA recall and winning removal of the import alert.
scores.quote: the company gives utmost importance to food safety and compliance with regulatory requirements and leaves no stone unturned

scores.rationale: Only the nascent pet-care business discusses reach (Tier-1 to Tier-3 cities, Amazon, Supertails); the calls say almost nothing about the feed dealer network or farmer-facing sales force that would evidence real customer intimacy.
scores.quote: strengthening its presence in Tier-1 cities and has initiated expansion into Tier-2 and Tier-3 markets

scores.rationale: The mix is fragmented farmers (who get reliability but no lock-in) plus US corporate importers where price and tariff, not switching costs, decide the sale — an imperfect match of benefit to customer type.
scores.quote: export volumes to the U.S. declined by 17.9%, whereas export to China increased by 24%

scores.rationale: No proprietary multi-product technology edge — pet-food formulations are licensed from Thailand and the fish-feed plan begins with importing others' product for trials.
scores.quote: The company is considering various options such as import of fish feed of required species initially, conduct trials under Indian conditions

scores.rationale: Nothing in the business model is two-sided or self-reinforcing; feed volumes track pond stocking and weather, not any network that strengthens with scale.
scores.quote: the status of aquaculture activity conditions such as climate, diseases, etc., determine the consumption of feed in terms of volume

scores.rationale: Roughly half of all Indian shrimp feed volume moves through the company's channel year after year, an installed reach across the aqua belt that rivals have not displaced despite cheaper imports.
scores.quote: The company's feed sales during FY22 was about 5.41 lakh MT... expected to maintain its market share to 48% - 50%

scores.rationale: Capex is overwhelmingly growth-oriented — 102 new stores added in three years versus 105 built in the prior 23 years — with store-level economics (6-month breakeven, 3-year payback) and ROCE/ROE of 28%/60% indicating high incremental returns, though a portion goes to renovation of older stores.
scores.quote: We have added 102 stores in the last 3 years, which is almost equal to 105 stores where we built in the previous 23 to 24 years.

scores.rationale: A&P is rising deliberately to seed new geographies (UP/Lucknow marketing, loyalty program 'Buy and Win', onboarding Pankaj Tripathi as brand ambassador) and is described as investment for market depth, but it has visibly compressed margins with returns still unproven.
scores.quote: we onboarded our brand ambassador also during this period as well as we were... entering new geographies... These are onetime expenses, but it gives us a lot of depth in market

scores.rationale: As a pure OEM-product retailer with no private label, R&D is never discussed in any call.
No acquisition is mentioned anywhere across the 13 calls; growth is entirely organic store rollout.
Capital actions have been liquidity/growth-oriented — a 10:1 stock split, NSE listing, ESOPs and an equity fundraise — with no buyback or articulated distribution policy discussed.
scores.quote: we have completed stock split in 10:1 ratio... our shares have now been listed on NSE for Trading as well as giving investors more liquidity

scores.rationale: Returns are high (ROCE 28%, ROE 60%) on a leased-store model, but the balance sheet is inventory-heavy by design (INR840 crores inventory on INR2,672 crores revenue, ~80 days) and debt-funded, so it is high-return rather than genuinely asset-light.
scores.quote: The ROCE and ROE for the year were 28% and 60% respectively.

scores.rationale: Demonstrated capture — ~60% share in Bihar and 15% in Jharkhand within two years — with large remaining runway (present in only 24 of 75 UP districts) and share taken during an industry slowdown.
scores.quote: Bihar, we have already, as per manufacturers, we have already captured around 60% of markets. And in Jharkhand, in only 2 years of operation, we have captured nearly 15%.

scores.rationale: A methodically sequenced contiguous-state expansion (Bihar 1999-2021, Jharkhand FY22, Eastern then Central UP, Chhattisgarh ahead of plan, MP next) executed with zero store closures since inception.
scores.quote: we close FY26 with 207 stores across 4 states... We have entered Chhattisgarh earlier than planned with 3 stores

scores.rationale: Growth is volume- and store-count-led, not price/mix-led: ASPs fell across categories, mix shifted toward low-margin mobiles/laptops, and FY26 gross margin declined ~100bps year-on-year.
scores.quote: ASP has gone down due to decrease in most of the categories, especially AC, refrigerator, washers. It has gone down by 2%.

scores.rationale: FY26 saw the weakest summer since inception depressing the high-margin cooling category, and management has stocked aggressively against clear signals of a normal-to-strong summer ahead — a plausible cyclical trough with an identifiable upturn.
scores.quote: despite this year having the weakest summer since our inception... with clear signals of a strong summer ahead, we ensure that we are fully stocked

scores.rationale: The end market is structurally under-penetrated Tier 2-4 Hindi heartland with rising disposable incomes and improving power availability, which management cites as the durable driver of high SSSG.
scores.quote: we are operating in a very under-penetrated market. That is why SSG will remain high... demand will continue to come here.

scores.rationale: Purely organic, cluster-led expansion with explicit store-economics discipline, counter-cyclical investment (36 stores added during COVID; opportunistic AC buying), but leverage is real (net debt/EBITDA 1.39x, net debt/equity 1.40x) and working capital is stretched.
scores.quote: one of the key reasons for downfall of retail companies has been excessive growth and deteriorating unit economics. Hence, we believe in calibrated expansion

scores.rationale: A 27-year, first-generation-entrepreneur-built business that raised only INR5.8 crores at IPO and no further funds for years, consolidated Bihar for 22 years before moving out, and refuses to follow fashions (no online, no rushed AI adoption).
scores.quote: In 2016, when we had 16 showrooms, we came out with an IPO and raised 5.8 crores... Since this issue, we have not raised any fund till date.

scores.rationale: Management is understated and operations-focused — the maiden call came only in 2023 after 24 years, and commentary stays on store economics and geography rather than self-promotion — though the recent celebrity brand ambassador and NSE listing raise the profile somewhat.
scores.quote: I welcome all the participants to this inaugural earnings call of Aditya Vision. As this is our maiden call

scores.rationale: ESOPs were distributed broadly to over 300 employees down to cashiers and warehouse staff, culture is explicitly owned by the MD, and an industry veteran was added to the board, but there is little evidence of a formal succession pipeline beyond the promoter family.
scores.quote: we have granted ESOPs to over 300 employees, widely distributed to include not just senior-level executives but also store managers, cashiers, warehouse and service executives

scores.rationale: Management confronts bad news directly — admitting the industry slowdown, calling Q1 FY26 'a total washout', explaining margin compression line by line and rebutting governance allegations — but repeatedly declines granular disclosure (state-wise margins, inventory quantum, bank interest rates) and brushed off a depreciation query.
scores.quote: do not forget that this year, Q1 was a total washout. So comparing that the biggest quarter of the company's history was a total washout.

scores.rationale: Headline growth is genuinely strong, but much of it comes from a structurally under-penetrated market and sheer store additions while SSSG fell to 5% for 9M FY26, margins compressed, and opex/inventory ballooned — so results should not be read as pure managerial skill.
scores.quote: Same-store sales growth for nine months FY '26 stood at 5%

scores.rationale: In Bihar the company holds ~60% share with an entrenched position in the customer's mind ('Sambandh Bharose Ka') plus a captive after-sales service arm, in a market with no organized competition.
scores.quote: It offers a large and underpenetrated consumer market and absence of organized competition.

scores.rationale: A clear regional monopoly in Bihar reinforced by an in-house service call centre and OEM billing relationships, though consumer-electronics retail carries weak formal switching costs.
scores.quote: We take pride in our dedicated customer service call center called Aditya Seva with a team of over 30 skilled employees

scores.rationale: The structure is not an oligopoly but one organized player against a long tail of small unorganized dealers, and management notes rising OEM competition rather than a stable few-player market.
scores.quote: it's good that many companies have established themselves in this market

scores.rationale: National chains and brand stores stay out of these geographies by their own stated policy and promoter ownership is stable, but pricing rationality is not assured — the company's edge comes from buying cheaper to 'remain competitive all the time'.
scores.quote: brand store, I think in the geography where we are operating, it will be the last thing that these brand stores are going to come... they will be present only in metros

scores.rationale: The competitive field is small dealers who cannot match AVL's inventory buying or price positioning, and organized peers are absent from these states, leaving abundant share to take.
scores.quote: for smaller dealers, they may be having those inventories of earlier pricing. So we want to remain competitive all the time.

scores.rationale: The niche — Tier 3/4 towns of Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern UP — is one national capital and OEM-owned retail deliberately ignore, though the NSE listing and coverage by IIFL, Investec, Axis and Emkay mean it is no longer unnoticed by investors.
scores.quote: mostly we are present in Tier 2, Tier 3 and even Tier 4 cities, towns... these totally unpenetrated areas are going to give us very good results

scores.rationale: Gross margin is a thin ~15-16% and entirely mix-dependent — it fell when mobiles and laptops grew — indicating the retailer has little independent pricing power from image or brand.
scores.quote: in a basket where you have products of lower margin and these have grown because of sudden spurt in their prices, then obviously, entire margin of the basket will come down.

scores.rationale: The entire proposition is trust and reliability — the tagline 'Sambandh Bharose Ka', a dedicated grievance call centre, and zero store closures in 27 years including COVID — with customers buying certainty of service rather than lowest price.
scores.quote: we believe in building a relationship of trust with them as our tagline symbolizes, Sambandh Bharose Ka.

scores.rationale: Accessibility is the core advantage: 207 stores placed inside district headquarters and small towns where customers prefer to see and feel goods, making the store visit a family occasion that online and quick commerce have not displaced.
scores.quote: in this part of India, people prefer seeing goods and feeling it. And it is like a family affair going to a store and buying.

scores.rationale: The customer base is purely retail and the benefit set is correctly matched — trust, hospitality, service and physical accessibility — rather than corporate-style TCO selling, though the retail intangible is service-based rather than aspirational.
scores.quote: Our success can be attributed to our unwavering commitment to a customer-centric approach.

scores.rationale: There is no technology edge — an ERP migration is the main system investment, the company has explicitly declined to build an online channel, and it is deliberately non-committal on AI.
scores.quote: Aditya Vision is not thinking about having online market as a whole.

scores.rationale: The single-sided, offline, own-store retail model with no marketplace or platform has no self-reinforcing network dynamic; scale benefits come from OEM buying power, not network effects.
scores.quote: Our business model focuses solely on pure retailing of products purchased from original equipment manufacturers (OEM) and we do not engage in private labels.

scores.rationale: The 207-store network across 38 Bihar districts, 22 of 24 Jharkhand districts and 30 UP districts, backed by OEM support for expansion and an in-house service arm, is reach no rival in these states can replicate.
scores.quote: We are now present with 118 stores in Bihar across 38 districts, 33 in Jharkhand covering 22 out of 24 districts, 53 in Uttar Pradesh

scores.rationale: Capex is overwhelmingly growth-directed (seats 110k in FY24 to 184k signed by FY26, 41 new centers in FY26) and incremental returns are exceptional, with ROCE rising from 43% to 62% and sustaining above 60% while the balance sheet stayed net cash.
scores.quote: Our return on capital employed also improved, rising from 43% in FY '24 to 62% in FY '25

scores.rationale: A&P is referenced only as one channel within a broader sales approach, with no spend disclosure, efficiency metric or evidence of durable brand equity being bought with it.
scores.quote: Our multi-channel approach of engaging real estate brokerages, digital media, advertising strategies and our in-house team

scores.rationale: No formal R&D line, but consistent product development (Design 6.0, VR walkthroughs, TechLabs, Frame furniture) has repeatedly converted into new revenue verticals and higher conversion.
scores.quote: we plan to launch our updated design, Design 6.0, to meet with the evolving needs of today's modern workforce

scores.rationale: Across all nine calls no acquisition is discussed; growth is entirely organic with partnerships (Eco Mobility, contract manufacturers) rather than M&A.
No dividend or buyback policy is mentioned in any call; the company is deploying IPO proceeds and internal accruals into growth.

The managed-aggregation model pushes fit-out capital onto space owners, delivering 60%+ ROCE on a net-cash balance sheet, and the micro-market clustering plus 26-month lock-ins provide at least a partial protective moat.
scores.quote: we are an end-to-end workplace solutions provider built on an asset-light, high-margin model

scores.rationale: Awfis is the largest flex operator yet flex is still only ~21% of Indian office leasing, and seats grew from 110,540 (FY24) to ~184,000 signed (FY26), well ahead of market growth.
scores.quote: As India's largest flexible workspace provider

scores.rationale: Credible, well-executed domestic expansion into 18 cities and nine Tier-2 markets with Tier-2 capacity up 16% y/y, but the footprint is India-only with no evidence the brand travels abroad.
scores.quote: We have expanded into high potential Tier 2 cities such as Guwahati and Lucknow

scores.rationale: Growth has been volume-led (seat additions) but the mix is now deliberately shifting to price/realization via premiumization, Grade A/A+ only supply and contractual 5-7% escalations.
scores.quote: our supply additions are now increasingly optimized for revenue per seat rather than headline seat count

scores.rationale: The company is riding near a cyclical peak, not a trough — CY2025 was the third consecutive record year of office leasing and Grade A completions also peaked.
scores.quote: CY 2025 saw record office leasing of 82.6 million square feet. The third consecutive record year

scores.rationale: The end market is in genuine secular expansion, with flex penetration rising from 5% to 21% and GCCs (20-30 first-time entrants per quarter) expected to be ~40% of office absorption.
scores.quote: penetration rising from 5% to 21% and expect it to reach 25% by 2027

scores.rationale: Purely organic growth, no acquisitions, negative net debt sustained through a heavy expansion phase, and a stated shift toward capital-light forward leasing and shared-capex developer partnerships.
scores.quote: delivered industry-leading returns on capital and stayed net cash through it all

scores.rationale: Founder-led since 2015 with a consistently executed multi-year shift to managed aggregation (46% of seats in FY21 to 66% in FY24) and FY25 revenue beating its own 30% guidance, though the FY26 design-and-build shortfall tempers the record.
scores.quote: We have increased the percentage of seats under the Managed Aggregation model from 46% in FY '21 to 66% in FY '24

scores.rationale: Commentary is markedly promotional and narrative-driven — 'defining year', 'five engines', 'compounding flywheel', 'dominant player' — rather than low-key and substance-first.
scores.quote: FY26 has been a defining year for Awfis

scores.rationale: Both key succession events were internal promotions — Deputy CEO Sumit Lakhani elevated to CEO and Head of Finance Sumit Rochlani to CFO — alongside deliberate senior hiring into enterprise sales and D&B leadership.
scores.quote: Having previously served as Head of Finance at Awfis, he brings valuable continuity and deep understanding of the business

scores.rationale: Management sets explicit guidance and reports against it, discloses IGAAP-equivalent numbers alongside Ind-AS, and openly flags the design-and-build shortfall and its causes, though with a promotional gloss.
scores.quote: FY '26 was a softer year on overall D&B revenue, driven by project timing and lower count of managed aggregation deals

scores.rationale: Headline results are heavily flattered by an exceptional cycle and by Ind-AS 116 lease accounting — 36.8% reported EBITDA margin versus ~14% normalized and only INR71 crores PAT on INR1,493 crores revenue — so skill is hard to separate from tailwind.
scores.quote: the normalized operating EBITDA stood at Rs.55 crores... margins stood at 36.5%

scores.rationale: Awfis holds a genuinely differentiated position in the operationally intensive small-cohort segment where no other large-scale operator competes, though this is niche leadership rather than monopoly.
scores.quote: Awfis is the only large-scale player in India with a strong presence in small cohort co-working segments

scores.rationale: Real but limited switching costs exist via 26-month lock-ins, 37-month average tenures and multi-center consolidation (48% of clients across multiple centers), yet clients can re-tender at renewal and rivals occupy the same micro-markets.
scores.quote: Average client tenure has strengthened to 37 months with lock-in tenure at 26 months

scores.rationale: The flex-workspace market is fragmented and openly competitive rather than a stable oligopoly, and large enterprise/GCC customers hold meaningful negotiating power.
scores.quote: Despite the competitive nature of the market, we have continued to deliver profitable growth

scores.rationale: Barriers are low — flex operators took ~23% of all leasing and capital keeps entering — and pricing is set by micro-market rentals rather than by operator discipline, leaving little pricing autonomy.
scores.quote: the pricing is a direct reflection of the overall micro market rental at that point of time

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly cites operational intensity as a barrier smaller operators cannot match, but never identifies specific weak competitors losing share to Awfis.
scores.quote: This is a highly operational-intensive business. It requires years of execution, capability, strong processes

scores.rationale: This is a high-visibility IPO story in a well-covered sector, with calls hosted by IIFL, Ambit and Asian Markets and active coverage from Avendus Spark — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: We recently concluded our IPO of INR 599 crores

scores.rationale: Premiumization, design awards and WELL certifications support image-led realization and 5-7% contractual escalations, but the underlying normalized margin (~14%) shows pricing power is moderate, not exceptional.
scores.quote: we also became the first coworking brand in India to achieve three WELL certifications

scores.rationale: Enterprise and GCC clients explicitly buy certainty — speed-to-market, compliance readiness and scalability — with first-time GCCs described as highly sticky and long-term rather than price-driven.
scores.quote: clients are looking for speed, compliance, scalability, and long-term flexibility

scores.rationale: 250 centers across 18 cities with deep micro-market density plus in-house sales, broker channels and bundled allied services (café, IT, transport, events) give unmatched accessibility and client intimacy.
scores.quote: Outer Ring Road in Bangalore alone houses 12 of our centers

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is well matched to a predominantly corporate base — 64% large corporates/MNCs buying reliability and lock-in — while the small-cohort co-working funnel feeds retail-type users into that pipeline.
scores.quote: Enterprise and MNC clients now account for 64% of our client base

scores.rationale: Technology is a useful operating aid (Expiry 90 renewal tool, VR walkthroughs, TechLabs IT arm) but there is no deep multi-product tech edge or R&D intensity underpinning the business.
scores.quote: Awfis TechLabs launched in FY '25 is our integrated IT service arm

scores.rationale: There is a real but one-sided density effect — 48% of clients operate across multiple centers and clustering lowers risk and opex — rather than a self-reinforcing two-sided network.
scores.quote: This clustering creates network effects that are very difficult to replicate

scores.rationale: Pan-India reach of 250 centers across 18 cities with multiple formats co-located in the same catchment lets Awfis serve national workspace consolidation mandates no smaller rival can match.
scores.quote: When a client expands from one center to multiple centers across cities, they are not just renewing a contract, they are choosing Awfis as their national operating partner

scores.rationale: Steady growth capex (IPO-funded Bundi wheat unit, Krishnapatnam oleo line, specialty chemicals) but capacity utilisation of only ~63% and thin ~3–3.5% EBITDA margins imply modest incremental ROIC.
scores.quote: our new installation coming up at Krishnapatnam by end of early Q1 of -- Q4 of '27 should be able to add more volume to this segment

scores.rationale: Sustained, rising A&P and BTL spend across 14 quarters coincides with Fortune brand growth of 11–13% and edible-oil share moving 18.4%→19.5%, though food-segment profits are consumed by the spend.
scores.quote: We stepped up brand investment during the quarter with multiple new advertising campaigns launched across the region.

scores.rationale: No R&D spend or pipeline is ever discussed; product work is formulation/marketing-led launches (Pehli Dhaar, expert range, Premio, specialty flours) with no evidence of R&D efficiency.
scores.quote: We launched our new series Fortune Premio, our premium brand in the -- under which we launched Olive Oil and also launched Cold Press Mustard Oil.

scores.rationale: Bolt-ons are small and complementary — Kohinoor (2022) recovered to 32–39% growth and GD Foods (2025) held its 54% material margin while scaling on AWL's distribution — though Kohinoor took ~3 years to turn.
scores.quote: when we took over G.D. Foods, the material margins were actually in the range of 50% kind of margins. We have actually -- while scaling up the business, we have been able to retain this margin

scores.rationale: Buybacks, dividends or any distribution policy are never mentioned in the excerpts.
Turnover is high in absolute terms (₹74,000 cr revenue) but the base is crushing/refining plants running at only ~63% utilisation with ~10% gross margins and no protecting moat on the asset base.
scores.quote: The capacities utilizations are at a reasonably good level , 63%

scores.rationale: Consistent share capture with ample runway — edible oil 18.4%→19.5% (+60bps in Q4FY26), basmati 5.1%→~9–11.9%, wheat flour 5%→5.9% — but wheat flour share stalled at 5.3–5.4% by FY26.
scores.quote: one significant improvement, which we saw in the basmati rice where our market share improved by 330 basis points

scores.rationale: Branded exports scaled from an initiative in 2022 to 30+ countries growing 36–48% y/y, plus improving Bangladesh subsidiary and rural town coverage from 30,000 to 63,000 towns.
scores.quote: Branded export which is also a focus area of Company for last couple of years now, we are exporting to over 30 countries now

scores.rationale: Growth is volume- and commodity-price-pass-through led, with industry-wide grammage cuts (1000g→750g) and consumer down-trading rather than pricing/mix gains; premiumisation remains a small metro-only initiative.
scores.quote: competition started reducing the weight so as to reduce the price. And it started from 1000 grams, to say, 900 and then 850, then 800, then 750.

scores.rationale: The edible oil complex is at elevated, not trough, levels at the end of the window — sunflower above $1,400/t after the Iran conflict, with input costs (packing, chemicals, coal) yet to hit Q1FY27.
scores.quote: edible oil prices flared up, particularly in the month of Mar ch after the conflict started with sunflower settling above $1,400 a ton

scores.rationale: Branded staples penetration in India is structurally expanding, evidenced by 11+ quarters of ~30% food growth and alternate/quick-commerce channels compounding at 42–65% y/y.
scores.quote: Quick commerce volume grew by a robust 65% year-on-year during the quarter.

scores.rationale: Predominantly organic build with only small bolt-ons and explicitly non-speculative risk management, though the FY24 hedge dis-alignment showed the discipline is not foolproof.
scores.quote: given the fact that our positions are not speculative in nature, and therefore, we -- and that is the basis at which we are giving this estimate

scores.rationale: Multi-year tenacity is visible: distribution built from 740k to 970k direct outlets, HoReCa and branded exports nurtured over several years, and food openly kept in an investment phase for another 2–3 years.
scores.quote: this business will still remain in an investment phase or a growth phase as we go forward

scores.rationale: Executives themselves are operational and low-key, but the company carried the highly visible Adani name for most of the period and is India's largest, most-covered edible oil player.
scores.quote: we are there , and we are the largest spenders of edible oil for sure

scores.rationale: Leadership transitions were internal — CFO Kanhere elevated to MD & CEO and Mallick/Sheth moved up to Deputy Chairman and ED — indicating a working pipeline, though the CFO seat sits with an interim.
scores.quote: MR. SHRIKANT KANHERE – MANAGING DIRECTOR AND CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER
