scores.quote: is there an import risk from China that China will dump at lower prices in India?

scores.rationale: A genuinely unglamorous Solapur-based amines niche with thin analyst coverage (single broker-hosted calls, individual investors asking questions) and products most capital ignores.
scores.quote: Rajeev Rupani, an individual investor

scores.rationale: No image or taste-based pricing power — margins swing 17.5% to 25% purely with methanol and ammonia, and management itself frames the sustainable band as input-cost-determined.
scores.quote: with a reasonable EBITDA, we should be in a position to maintain 20% to 22%. And with the lowest, it should be 17.5% to 18%

scores.rationale: Customers do buy supply certainty — the company maintained uninterrupted supply through the March 2026 geopolitical disruption when peers shut down, backed by BIS certification and multi-year US/Europe contract renewals.
scores.quote: This enabled us to maintain supplies to customers and ensure that plant operations remained stable

scores.rationale: There is regional accessibility to Maharashtra and southern customers and direct plant visits by prospects, but no evidence of a distinctive sales force or customer-intimacy advantage.
scores.quote: there are 1 or 2 companies who visited the plant and who we have seen are serious

scores.rationale: Customers are entirely corporate (pharma, agrochem, battery makers) and the company does offer reliability and qualification-based lock-in, but those TCO benefits proved insufficient to stop a major customer integrating backwards.
scores.quote: one of your pharma customers, they have backward integrated into methylamines for captive consumption

scores.rationale: Real indigenous process capability across a multi-product portfolio — a self-developed low-cost acetonitrile route, backward-integrated methylamine-DMF chain and electronic-grade purity — but R&D intensity is not high enough to be a deep edge.
scores.quote: as per the latest technology, we are going to produce the very high-purity material at a low-cost -- manufacturing cost

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic exists or is discussed in a bulk chemicals business.
Distribution is ordinary B2B direct supply with ISO tanks and export agents; management cites customer relationships and supply chain but shows no reach rivals cannot replicate.
scores.quote: we have given already couple of ISO Tanks to the various customers in the Europe

scores.rationale: Capex is large, growth-oriented and rising across the period (carbon black 265k MTPA, Bhuj power to 64MW, CV radial Phase 1 at INR750cr, PCR, INR2,800cr spent in FY26 and a further INR2,000cr approved to FY29), but incremental returns are unproven since revenue was flat and FY26 EBITDA fell 10%.
scores.quote: The Board of Directors has approved an additional capex of INR2,000 crores

scores.rationale: Sustained, scaling brand investment — IPL, an all-five-team Women's Premier League deal, Ranveer Singh as ambassador and a brand-architecture repositioning — with management citing brand positioning as what let it regain US momentum, though A&P has not yet translated into revenue growth.
scores.quote: BKT Tires is the offici al partner with all the five women's IPL teams

scores.rationale: New products do emerge (TBR, 2-wheeler, PCR, specialty carbon black grades approved for plastics, pressure pipes, cables and inks) but management says development spend is immaterial and never discusses R&D intensity or efficiency.
scores.quote: Nothing significant to note -- I mean, to highlight over here.

scores.rationale: No acquisitions in the period — management explicitly stands aside from European sector M&A and from any China JV, so growth is wholly organic with no deal record to judge.
scores.quote: on M&A, there is no impact, as we have mentioned. We are also waiting and watching.

scores.rationale: A consistent, predictable quarterly dividend policy (INR4/share each quarter, INR16 for FY26) maintained through the downcycle, but there are no buybacks and no valuation-linked distribution discipline.
scores.quote: recommended a final dividend of INR4 per equity share

scores.rationale: The business is structurally asset-heavy — INR2,800cr of capex in FY26 against INR10,656cr of standalone revenue, with a further INR6,800cr programme to FY29 and backward integration into carbon black and captive power.
scores.quote: Our capex spend for the year was INR2,800 crores approximately.

scores.rationale: Ample runway remains as a value challenger to Tier-1s, and India is gaining, but US volumes fell ~30% YoY on tariffs and management denied any China-to-India share shift, so the recent record is share defence rather than capture.
scores.quote: we are trying to just regain some of the lost momentum that we had in Q2

scores.rationale: The geographic footprint (Europe ~44%, India ~29%, Americas ~16%) is long-established rather than expanding; the only new initiative is a sharper Americas go-to-market after tariff-driven losses, with mix shifting toward lower-ASP India.
scores.quote: We have created a sharper focus in our go-to-market strategy for Americas

scores.rationale: FY26 delivered record volumes yet flat revenue, meaning growth was volume-led with negative price/mix (India mix dilutes ASP), and price hikes of 3-5% are reactive raw-material and tariff pass-through, part of which BKT absorbs.
scores.quote: registering flattish performance on a year-on-year basis

scores.rationale: The trajectory shows a full destocking cycle from FY23 through FY25 weakness into visible recovery — channel inventories normalized, Europe rebounding, US tariff refunds filed, H2 FY26 materially better than H1 with record Q4 volumes.
scores.quote: H2 performance was significantly better than H1.

scores.rationale: Core off-highway agri/OTR demand is cyclical and GDP-like rather than secularly expanding (9M FY26 volumes were down 1% YoY), and the new TBR/PCR adjacency is a mature, crowded market despite radialization tailwinds.
scores.quote: This segment is aligned with infrastructure growth, increasing radialization trends

scores.rationale: Purely organic, no M&A, leverage kept modest (net debt INR895cr against INR3,154cr cash) and heavy counter-cyclical capex sustained straight through the downturn, though the scale of diversification capex into on-highway adds execution risk.
scores.quote: we have a net debt of INR895 crores

scores.rationale: A stated 2030 vision (INR5,000cr on-highway revenue) has been reiterated and methodically executed in phases — carbon black, CV radial Phase 1 completed Feb '26, 2-wheeler relaunch, PCR next — while refusing short-term guidance.
scores.quote: we are quite confident of keeping our long-term vision of 2030

scores.rationale: Promoter-family management runs short, factual calls, consistently declines to speculate or self-promote, and delegates detail to the CFO/deputy CFO; the celebrity spend is on the brand, not on the executives.
scores.quote: we cannot speculate on that

scores.rationale: The senior bench has visibly broadened beyond the promoter across the period — Satish Sharma added as Director Strategy, Bajaj elevated to Director Commercial, a Deputy CFO and Head of Accounts now on calls — plus an INR25cr BKT School of Engineering skilling commitment.
scores.quote: MR. SATISH SHARMA – SENIOR PRESIDENT AND DIRECTOR, STRATEGY AND BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT

scores.rationale: Disclosure of headline financials, weak demand and margin pressure is honest and consistent, but management repeatedly refuses to quantify tariff impact, US realizations and segment margins, lacks basic numbers on call, and has withdrawn guidance entirely.
scores.quote: I'm not able to quantify it on a public call because these are business details.

scores.rationale: Separating skill from outcome, the record is mixed: FY26 EBITDA fell 10% and PAT is well below FY23-25 peaks despite record volumes, and margin defence leaned on euro hedges (INR85 to INR97) and mix as much as on operating skill.
scores.quote: registering a degrowth of 10% on a year-on-year basis

scores.rationale: BKT is a value challenger positioned at a persistent discount to Tier-1 rather than owning the customer's mind, and it had to absorb part of the US tariff to hold shelf space.
scores.quote: the difference between us and the Tier 1 yet continues to be the same

scores.rationale: A 70-73% replacement-channel mix gives some aftermarket annuity, but there is no evidence of switching costs — distributors negotiate tariff sharing and volumes swing with channel destocking.
scores.quote: 73% was contributed from replacement segment

scores.rationale: Global OHT is a consolidating few-player market with visible European M&A, yet the distributor customer clearly retains negotiating power given tariff-cost sharing and BKT's inability to pass through full raw-material inflation.
scores.quote: we have shared with di stributors, but the large portion is being borne by them

scores.rationale: Capital intensity and SKU complexity keep entrants out, pricing behaviour has stayed rational through a deep destocking cycle with no discount war, promoter ownership is stable, and the PCR entry is explicitly non-discounted.
scores.quote: we are not discounting our products. We'll be in line with the market leaders.

scores.rationale: Western Tier-1 competitors face structurally higher cost bases and production stoppages in Europe, giving BKT a clear cost-advantaged pool of share to take.
scores.quote: Their costs have also gone up being in the western world.

scores.rationale: Off-highway tyres is a genuine niche, but BKT is a widely covered large cap with heavy IPL and celebrity-ambassador visibility and multiple sell-side analysts on every call — the opposite of under-the-radar.
scores.quote: further strengthening our brand visibility

scores.rationale: Margins near 23% and brand-driven US recovery show some pricing power, but BKT prices below Tier-1, absorbs tariff and raw-material costs, and margins compressed 25.6% to 22.7% over the period.
scores.quote: The margin, however, stood at 22.7%

scores.rationale: Management attributes regained US volumes to product quality and reliability reputation rather than price, and EUDR-readiness ahead of regulation shows customers buying certainty of supply.
scores.quote: our strong product quality, brand positioning

scores.rationale: A deep multi-country distributor network underpins the 73% replacement business, and the company rapidly built ~90 primary distributors for its new on-highway range with dealerships scaling behind sales.
scores.quote: The primary distribution in the form of distributors is nearly complete for both the categories

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is well matched — retail-facing replacement channel supported by mass brand-building (IPL, Ranveer Singh) while OEM/corporate customers are served on quality, compliance readiness and range.
scores.quote: 73% was contributed from replacement segment , while OEM contributed to 25%

scores.rationale: Backward integration into specialty carbon black with grade approvals and AI-enabled automation capex show real capability, but there is no disclosed R&D intensity and the new TBR/PCR segments are technologically commoditized.
scores.quote: we have already secured approvals for select grades across plastics, pressure pi pes, and power cables and inks

scores.rationale: No evidence of any two-sided or self-reinforcing network is discussed across the calls.

Distribution breadth across Europe, Americas, India and rest-of-world is the core asset — it absorbed a multi-quarter destocking cycle and was leveraged to place entirely new product categories within months.
scores.quote: We are about 90 in all for these categories

scores.rationale: Large, clearly growth-oriented capex — distillery expansion to 1,050 KLPD, then the ₹3,080 crore PLA plant and a ₹160 crore lactogypsum board plant — but incremental ROIC is unproven (cost overrun of ₹230 crore, 5-year payback on the by-product plant).
scores.quote: there has been a cost overrun of INR230 crore, taking the project cost to INR3,080 crore from INR2,850 crore

scores.rationale: Across four years there is no brand-building spend; management explicitly wants to avoid it even for its one consumer-facing product, gypsum boards.
scores.quote: we do not want to sort of get into some big-time branding expense

scores.rationale: Consistent applied R&D — tissue culture, varietal rebalancing away from Co0238 that brought red rot under control, and grade/barrier development work for PLA — though the core PLA technology is licensed from Sulzer rather than developed in-house.
scores.quote: we have a big team which is dealing with Sulzer, which is the technology supplier

scores.rationale: No acquisitions at all over the period; the only non-organic holding is an unrelated NBFC (Auxilo) that management now intends to exit, so there is neither a bolt-on track record nor value destruction.
scores.quote: Definitely, eventually yes, 100%.

scores.rationale: Early stance was returning surplus cash, but by FY26 the company is issuing ₹450 crore of preferential equity at ₹483 (5% dilution) rather than distributing — promoters at least subscribed pro-rata to keep stake at 43%.
scores.quote: continued participation from the promoters in the fundraise will keep our stake, the family stake, at 43%

scores.rationale: Deeply asset-heavy: crushing, distillery and now a ₹3,080 crore plant for only 80,000 tonnes of PLA, with cane, sugar and ethanol economics all fixed-cost-absorption driven.
scores.quote: The reduction in crushing days further contributed to under-absorption of fixed overhead.

scores.rationale: Clear share capture in its home state — Balrampur crushed 5.2% more cane in SS2025-26 while all of UP crushed 7% less, from a non-dominant ~12% UP base leaving runway.
scores.quote: UP crushed 7% lower cane than last year and we have crushed 5.2% higher cane

scores.rationale: Footprint stays anchored in the UP cane belt; exports are entirely government-permission dependent and even the new gypsum board market is scoped to UP/North.
scores.quote: More like, UP and North

scores.rationale: Growth is volume- and policy-driven, not price- or mix-led: sugar prices are bounded by government MSP and ethanol prices have been frozen for three years while cane cost rose ₹30/quintal.
scores.quote: the absence of revision of ethanol prices under the juice and B-heavy route for the last 3 years, despite higher cane costs

scores.rationale: By FY26 the company sits near a favourable point of the sugar cycle — lowest inventory in management's memory, firm ₹41-42/kg UP prices, and high crude improving both ethanol economics and PLA's competitiveness versus fossil plastic.
scores.quote: probably this is the lowest stock level which I remember seeing in my recent living memory

scores.rationale: Genuine secular end-market pull from the ethanol blending programme (1.5%→10%→20% target) and now bioplastic mandates at Centre and UP level, tempered by the demonstrated policy fragility (Dec 2023 diversion ban, frozen prices).
scores.quote: there are three fronts: the Central Government mandate, the UP Government mandate, and customers

scores.rationale: Organic-only growth, no M&A, project funded from internal accruals plus modest debt at 6.75%, and the equity raise was framed explicitly around protecting ratings and rating headroom rather than empire building.
scores.quote: maintain our credit rating, and ensure financial stability, we are currently raising finance at around 6.75%

scores.rationale: A repeated pattern of early, independent long-horizon bets — India's first sugar co-generation plant, then pioneering PLA in India over a 4-year build, and now converting the PLA by-product rather than dumping it, with the co-gen precedent cited as the template.
scores.quote: We were India's first sugar factory to enter into a co-generation project, which later yielded rich dividends

scores.rationale: Management deliberately declines to publicise commercial wins and refuses to hype milestone announcements, preferring substance over news flow, though the promoter family is a visible presence on calls.
scores.quote: It is not proper to announce each and every agreement

scores.rationale: Functional teams (cane management, PLA/Sulzer team) are referenced, but leadership succession is family-based — Avantika Saraogi elevated to Executive Director — with no evidence of a systematic internal pipeline.
scores.quote: we have a big team which is dealing with Sulzer

scores.rationale: Repeatedly owns mistakes without spin — publicly admits its cane guidance failed, refuses to re-guess to protect credibility, and itemises the cost overrun including the portion it calls supplier blackmail.
scores.quote: our projection failed definately... Some are genuine, 90% are genuine, 10% is a bit of blackmail

scores.rationale: Results are heavily policy-determined (MSP, FRP/SAP, ethanol pricing, export bans), so skill is hard to isolate; the one clean skill signal is outperforming UP's crush by ~12 percentage points, which keeps the assessment neutral rather than flattering.
scores.quote: Ethanol unrestricted quantity, correct ethanol price as somebody put it, 2022-23 formula and MSP

scores.rationale: Core sugar/ethanol has no monopoly-like position in any customer's mind, but the first-in-India PLA plant could create one if the bioplastic mandates land — currently unproven.
scores.quote: being the first of its kind in the country

scores.rationale: The reserved cane command-area system gives a de facto regional monopsony over 3.24 lakh hectares of growers whom the company locks in via development, varietal supply and irrigation support.
scores.quote: We are reporting our cane area of 3.24 lakh hectares for the first time

scores.rationale: UP sugar is fragmented across many mills — Balrampur is only ~12% of state output — and the true price-setter is the government, not industry structure.
scores.quote: our share would be, roughly 12%

scores.rationale: Licensing and cane-area reservation keep new entrants out, and administered MSP/FRP pricing plus stable 43% promoter ownership preclude discount wars.
scores.quote: whatever is the MSP, let us take a figure of let's say, Rs.36.5/kg... UP makes a bottom at Rs.39/kg

scores.rationale: Weaker UP mills and the unorganised khandsari/gur/kolhu sector are visibly losing cane, and Balrampur has been the beneficiary in the season data.
scores.quote: we expect lesser diversion this year as compared to last year towards the unorganized Khandari, Kolhu Krusher sector

scores.rationale: Far from under-the-radar — calls are attended by mutual funds, family offices, multiple brokerages and CNBC TV18, and the PLA story attracts heavy investor attention.
scores.quote: The next question is from the line of Rhea Bhatia from CNBC TV18.

scores.rationale: Sugar, ethanol and gypsum boards are all commodities with no image- or taste-based pricing power; the realisation floor is set by government MSP and management sees no premium even for the eco-friendly attribute.
scores.quote: to attribute value based on that, I do not know if we will get more value

scores.rationale: Some trust-based positioning is emerging in PLA — customers have validated quality, food-contact safety and barrier properties before committing — but they still refuse to switch suppliers until commercial volumes and price are proven.
scores.quote: they are okay with our quality and they are waiting for the production to hit the market

scores.rationale: Deep intimacy exists on the supplier (farmer) side, not the customer side; the company has no downstream sales network and is only beginning to think about board distribution 18 months out.
scores.quote: So we are working on the sales strategy and in time to come, we will lay it out threadbare.

scores.rationale: Customers are corporate/bulk (OMC ethanol tenders, sugar trade, PLA converters, board dealers) but the offer carries no switching-cost lock-in — ethanol is re-tendered annually and PLA buyers keep incumbent suppliers.
scores.quote: They are not ready to replace their current supplier base with us, as of now.

scores.rationale: The PLA edge is licensed process technology plus feedstock/energy location advantage rather than proprietary multi-product tech, though full-chain integration from sugar to polymer is genuinely differentiated versus TotalEnergies Corbion's split structure.
scores.quote: TotalEnergies Corbion is not capturing the entire value addition in the manufacture of PLA

scores.rationale: Nothing in the model is self-reinforcing with scale — output is sold into commodity channels, government tenders and bulk converters, with no two-sided dynamic anywhere in four years of calls.
scores.quote: So, this is the way gypsum will come out. Either you dispose, throw, give to cement at dirt cheap rates

scores.rationale: No distribution advantage — sugar and ethanol move through trade and OMC tenders, and for gypsum boards management concedes rivals have the dealer portfolio while it may even white-label.
scores.quote: those companies have a portfolio to offer to the dealers which we would not have

scores.rationale: Real growth investment in branches and technology is visible (1,831 branches, CBS migration, rising IT spend), but the incremental return is poor with 9MFY26 RoE at 4% and the ROA aspiration pushed out.
scores.quote: taking the branch network to 1,831 branches, with 20 new branches added during the quarter and the conversion of 57 housing centres into full-fledged banking branches

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotion spend in any of the excerpts.
No R&D spend or R&D productivity is discussed; technology spend is disclosed only as an operating cost line.
No acquisitions are mentioned across the five-year span; only ARC portfolio sales, which are not M&A.
A token flat dividend with no buyback and no articulated distribution policy — neither disciplined value-creation nor a red flag.
scores.quote: a dividend of INR1.50 per equity share of INR10 for the year ended March 31, 2024, which is at the same level as the previous year

scores.rationale: The high-yield asset engine has structurally eroded — NIM fell from 8% in Q1FY23 to 6.2% in Q1FY27 as the book shifted to lower-yield secured lending, showing no protecting moat on returns.
scores.quote: margins remained stable at 6.2%

scores.rationale: Share is being lost in the core microfinance franchise (EEB down 11% YoY in Q3FY26) while non-EEB grows fast off a small base, so net share capture is unproven.
scores.quote: The EEB book stood at Rs 50,076 crores, showing a 11% YoY and 3% sequential decline

scores.rationale: Multi-year de-concentration away from West Bengal has been executed steadily, with deposit concentration falling and the branch/outlet footprint extended nationally.
scores.quote: It used to be 43% a year back down to 40% now.

scores.rationale: Growth is volume- and mix-driven in the wrong direction: the shift to secured lending compresses yields and NII grew only 6% YoY in Q1FY27 despite 16% advances growth.
scores.quote: the natural yield compression arising from the rising share of secured lending in the portfolio

scores.rationale: The bank appears past the trough of the microfinance credit cycle, with slippages falling, credit cost down to 1.8% from 3.4% in FY24, and EEB de-growth reversing.
scores.quote: the de-growth phase in EEB book is behind and the portfolio is stabilising with a more constructive trajectory going ahead

scores.rationale: Indian retail credit and formal financial inclusion remain in secular expansion, with management repeatedly citing a favourable BFSI macro backdrop and 3.35 crore customers added into the formal system.
scores.quote: The favourable macro backdrop should continue to help the momentum in the Indian BFSI sector in the coming quarters.

scores.rationale: Organic-only, well-capitalised (CAR 18.2%, Tier 1 17.5%) and conservatively provisioned, but the discipline was reactive — a INR3,852 crore technical write-off and repeated ARC sales followed years of under-recognised COVID-era stress.
scores.quote: the bank has done a technical write-off amounting to INR3,852 crores

scores.rationale: The diversification agenda has been pursued consistently since 2022 and is now delivering (non-EEB two-thirds of the book), but the founder's exit and wholesale replacement of the leadership team break continuity of vision.
scores.quote: The non-EEB portfolio grew by 27% YoY and now contributes 2/3 of the overall loan book

scores.rationale: Calls across all 17 quarters are plain, metric-heavy and free of celebrity positioning, with the founder's retirement handled procedurally through a board search process.
scores.quote: The Board in accordance with the Business Continuity Plan and the Succession Plan of the Bank has appointed a search firm

scores.rationale: The entire senior bench — COO, CBO, CFO, business heads and ultimately the MD/CEO — was hired externally in 2024, indicating no internal leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: During the last 3 months we have had several members of senior management joining the bank.

scores.rationale: Disclosure is granular (SMA buckets, one-off costs, ARC valuations at 9% and 18%) and the ROA guidance cut was made explicit, but the shortfall is attributed almost entirely to external factors and headline numbers are habitually re-presented on an 'adjusted' basis.
scores.quote: I again repeat that this is on account of the external factors that is affecting the economy of the country.

scores.rationale: There is no halo to strip away — reported returns are weak (9MFY26 RoA 0.5%, RoE 4%) and management's claimed skill is not corroborated by results, so the assessment rests on disclosed numbers rather than reputation.
scores.quote: For 9MFY26, RoA and RoE stood at 0.5% and 4%, respectively

scores.rationale: A historically strong mindshare position in East India group lending exists, but it is not monopoly-like — the EEB book shrank under competitive and credit pressure and no aftermarket lock-in is described.
scores.quote: West Bengal contributes to about 24% of the advances

scores.rationale: Regional density in West Bengal/Assam gives some local advantage, but switching costs are absent — rate-sensitive depositors left when savings rates were cut.
scores.quote: The lower rates led to an outflow of certain high-value, rate-sensitive balances

scores.rationale: Indian banking and microfinance are fragmented and price-competitive; management repeatedly frames its own difficulties as industry-wide rather than as an oligopolist setting terms.
scores.quote: the pressure on CASA is not unique to us. The industry as a whole has been witnessing similar challenges

scores.rationale: Low barriers and price-based competition are evident in funding costs and deposit pricing, with the bank forced to run down high-cost bulk deposits and cut savings rates while funding costs stayed elevated despite no repo hike.
scores.quote: the impact of higher funding costs despite no increase in the repo rate is already visible

scores.rationale: Bandhan has been the donator rather than the taker in its core segment, shrinking EEB and selling stressed pools while sector-wide microfinance stress hit it hardest.
scores.quote: We sold Rs 3,707 crores of written-off portfolio, which was realized at a valuation of roughly 9%

scores.rationale: This is a widely followed listed bank with dedicated IR and calls attended by CLSA, JM Financial and Dymon Asia — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: the first question from the line of Sameer Bhise from Dymon Asia

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power: yields and margins compress as the mix shifts, and depositors left on a modest savings-rate cut.
scores.quote: CASA deposits stood at Rs 42,730 crores, showing a 4% YoY decline

scores.rationale: Retail term deposits grew 36% YoY on stated customer trust, but the simultaneous rate-driven CASA outflow shows price, not assurance, still governs much of the franchise.
scores.quote: Retail term deposits continued their strong momentum, growing by over 36% YoY, underscoring the increasing trust of our customers

scores.rationale: Doorstep group-meeting collection with tablets, SMS acknowledgements, portable printers and flexible repayment tenures give genuine last-mile intimacy that few rivals replicate in these geographies.
scores.quote: real-time SMS acknowledgements for cash collections made during group meetings through our tablet-based system

scores.rationale: The retail micro-borrower base is served on convenience rather than intangibles, and the fast-growing wholesale book (33% of advances) is relationship-led without evidence of switching-cost lock-in.
scores.quote: Wholesale Banking also maintained strong momentum, growing 38% YoY, supported by deeper customer relationships

scores.rationale: Technology is a catch-up investment rather than an edge — the CBS migration caused teething issues and parallel-run costs, and payments capability is bought in via Razorpay, BillDesk and Cashfree.
scores.quote: there were certain initial teething issues, which were being tackled

scores.rationale: The model is branch-and-fieldforce distribution with no two-sided network described anywhere in five years of calls; scale brings cost, not self-reinforcing advantage.
scores.quote: We have more than 1,700 branches. In the last quarter, we have opened 53 branches.

scores.rationale: A 6,300-outlet, 1,831-branch network reaching 3.35 crore underserved rural and semi-urban customers, with housing centres being converted to full branches, is reach that most rivals cannot economically match in these regions.
scores.quote: Bandhan Bank has a strong network base of 6300 banking outlets & more than 3.35 crore customer base

scores.rationale: Investment is directed at growth platforms — the bob World digital build-out drove ~150% personal-loan growth and 22mn users within a year, and new subsidiaries (primary dealership, pension fund) were funded from internal accruals while ROE stayed 15-17%.
scores.quote: bob World now has 22 million users, and this is within 1 year

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend anywhere in the excerpts.
No R&D spend or R&D-productivity disclosure; IT/platform functions are mentioned only as organisational responsibilities.
No acquisitions are discussed across the four years; the only new businesses (BOB Securities and Giltedge, pension fund) were built organically, leaving nothing to judge on acquisition quality.
scores.quote: we created a primary dealer business in terms of creating a BOB's Securities and Giltedge Limited

scores.rationale: A dividend of Rs 8.5/share was declared for FY26 and growth has been self-funded from accruals without equity raising, but there is no buyback and no articulated distribution policy or valuation discipline.
scores.quote: Bank has declared a dividend of Rs. 8.5 per share, subject to requisite approvals.

scores.rationale: As a leveraged balance-sheet bank, asset turn is structurally low (ROA ~1.06-1.15%) and the earning-asset yield is falling (yield on advances 8.55% in FY25 Q1 to 7.37% in Q1FY27), with no moat protecting spreads.
scores.quote: yield on advances stands at 7.37 % for the quarter

scores.rationale: Advances growth of 16.2% FY26 and 17.4% in Q1FY27, with CASA growth described as better than peers, indicates share capture from a non-dominant position in a fragmented banking market.
scores.quote: our CASA has grown by 6%, which is better than the peer banks also

scores.rationale: International advances grew 24.4% and 23.3% YoY off a large existing overseas franchise, but the same international business produced the USD 600mn NMC settlement that wiped out a quarter's profit, so execution quality is mixed.
scores.quote: The liability of the Bank in these proceedings is limited to the sum of USD 600 million

scores.rationale: Growth is volume-led — yield on advances fell from 8.55% (Q1FY25) to 7.37% (Q1FY27) and NIM from 3.18% to 2.77% — only partially offset by favourable RAM/retail mix shift to 61%.
scores.quote: Our Net Interest Margin stands at 2.77 % for the quarter

scores.rationale: The bank sits near the top of the credit cycle, not the bottom — credit cost at 0.29%, GNPA 1.89% and SMA 0.07% are cycle-best levels that management itself buffers against with floating provisions, implying normalisation ahead.
scores.quote: credit cost is at 0.29 % and this talks about the asset quality the Bank is having in terms of a benign asset quality

scores.rationale: Indian credit demand is in secular expansion — retail crossed Rs 3 lakh crore, MSME grew 20.3% and total business crossed Rs 30 lakh crore — though growth is GDP-linked rather than a niche secular theme.
scores.quote: the Bank's global business volume has crossed the milestone of Rs. 30 lakh crores

scores.rationale: Consistently organic and prudent — deliberately shed bulk deposits and low-yield assets to protect margins, kept CET1 at 13-13.9%, and used an IT refund to create Rs 1,500cr of floating provisions rather than book the profit.
scores.quote: we thought it prudent to utilize this entire refund in creating a floating provision

scores.rationale: A stated priority hierarchy — asset quality, then profitability, then growth — has been held consistently for years and delivered (15+ quarters of >1% ROA, 13 quarters of >Rs 4,000cr profit), though as a PSU the bank's independence is inherently constrained.
scores.quote: we look at asset quality as the first piece and the profitability as the second and the top line is the third

scores.rationale: Management is career-banker, substance-first — MD and EDs present detailed operating metrics with no personality-driven narrative across all four calls.
scores.quote: let me again give some of the qualitative comments on the numbers that we have declared

scores.rationale: Internal pipeline is visible: Debadatta Chand was an Executive Director on the 2022 call and became MD & CEO by 2024, and the ED bench has been stable across the period, though PSU appointments are ultimately government-determined.
scores.quote: Mr. Debadatta Chand - Executive Director in charge of Corporate, International and Treasury

scores.rationale: Guidance is explicit and shortfalls are acknowledged, but candor is uneven — the bank declined to quantify the RBI investment-norm impact when peers did, and on NMC it reversed a stated intent to litigate while withholding the rationale as confidential.
scores.quote: the impact of the revised framework on the profit and loss account is not ascertained as the same are not comparable

scores.rationale: Headline record profits owe much to a benign credit cycle, IT refunds and reclassification benefits rather than demonstrable operating skill — NIM has compressed 40bps over the period and treasury income swung from Rs 2,200cr to Rs 800cr.
scores.quote: the treasury income in June '25 was almost more than 2,000 to 2,200 crores. Whereas it has gone down to 800 crores

scores.rationale: Commercial banking products here are undifferentiated commodities — the bank competes on price for both fine-priced corporate assets and deposits, with no monopoly position in any customer's mind.
scores.quote: there are certain low yielding assets, consciously we have shed it

scores.rationale: Switching costs are weak — deposits are openly contested and management repeatedly cites liability-side pressure and sticky market pricing it cannot control.
scores.quote: the liability is a challenge for all the banking industry

scores.rationale: Indian banking is crowded with PSU, private and small-finance players; customers hold negotiating power, evidenced by the bank's inability to reprice deposits and its yield give-up to retain corporate business.
scores.quote: the market condition at this level seems to be quite sticky with regard to the deposit pricing

scores.rationale: Licensing creates genuine entry barriers and ownership is stable, but pricing rationality is poor — the bank must walk away from business on price and competes hard for bulk and retail deposits.
scores.quote: the moment there is a bit of moderation happening, we'll again get into that market

scores.rationale: Weaker PSU peers are ceding ground — the bank's CASA and overall growth run ahead of peer banks and well ahead of system credit growth in FY26 and Q1FY27.
scores.quote: the CASA percentage, which is at 37.72%, you would have seen that it is one of the top quartile numbers

scores.rationale: This is one of India's largest banks with a Rs 30 lakh crore balance sheet, holding dedicated media and analyst meets each quarter with heavy sell-side coverage — the opposite of under-the-radar.
scores.quote: three banks are announcing their results today

scores.rationale: There is no image- or taste-driven pricing power; lending yields and margins are dictated by market liquidity and competition, with NIM guidance of just 2.75-2.95%.
scores.quote: All would depend upon the available liquidity in the scenario

scores.rationale: The sovereign-backed franchise buys depositor certainty — a 37-39% CASA ratio sustained through a tight liquidity cycle plus a deliberately over-provisioned balance sheet (PCR 93%+, floating provisions) sells safety over price.
scores.quote: it is a balance sheet strength we create and it is like a floating provision

scores.rationale: Accessibility is a genuine strength — the bob World mobile platform reached 38% active penetration of non-FI customers within a year and directly unlocked cross-sell of personal loans into the existing base.
scores.quote: with an efficient digital interface through bob World, we are able to access our customer base

scores.rationale: The mix is being tilted sensibly toward retail (RAM at 61%, retail book above Rs 3 lakh crore) while corporate remains reliability-driven, but neither side shows evidence of lock-in or benefit-specific pricing power.
scores.quote: the RAM growth has been good and the RAM percentage has gone to 61 %

scores.rationale: bob World is a competent, results-producing digital platform, but it is a catch-up-to-parity effort against private-bank standards rather than a deep multi-product technology edge.
scores.quote: which would pretty much bring us in line with the best in the business in terms of using mobile interface

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network is described anywhere; growth comes from balance-sheet deployment and cross-sell into an existing customer base, not from network scale.

Reach is a real advantage — a large domestic branch base plus one of the largest overseas footprints of any Indian bank, enabling offshore funding channels (FCNR, MTN, green bonds) peers cannot match.
scores.quote: Actually, we are one bank having a huge international presence.

scores.rationale: Sustained growth-oriented spend — a ~Rs.1,000 crore digital platform build promised in 2022 and delivered as the e-platform/BOI Omni Neo, plus 200 new branches each in FY25, FY26 and FY27 — accompanied by 16.6% business growth and 36% YoY profit growth in Q1FY27, though incremental returns remain modest (ROA ~0.7-0.9%).
scores.quote: we have already opened 200 new branches in FY 25, 200 branches were opened in this financial Year FY26 and another 200 plus branches will be opening in FY 27

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotion spend in any excerpt.

Digital product development is continuous but has run behind its own promises — 60-70 products were promised live within a month of Aug 2022 with a Sept 2023 deadline, yet by Aug 2024 only 25 were live with 15 still under development.
scores.quote: 25 products have been made live on the E-platform under RAM segment, with 15 more products under development

scores.rationale: Essentially no M&A other than a small consortium investment in CCIL-IFSC alongside six other banks, and management explicitly declined to engage on PSU bank consolidation.
scores.quote: along with other six banks, have come together and invested in the CCIL-IFSC Limited

scores.rationale: A routine dividend of roughly Rs.1,800-2,000 crore against Rs.10,527 crore net profit (~18% payout) with capital retained to build CRAR and absorb ECL; no buyback or articulated distribution policy.
scores.quote: even if we remove the net dividend also of around Rs.1800 to 2000 crores that we have to pay, still there accretion to Bank's net worth

scores.rationale: A balance-sheet-heavy PSU bank whose returns depend on leverage rather than asset turnover — ROA of only 0.70% and a global NIM that fell from 3.07% to 2.52% over the period.
scores.quote: The Return on Assets stood at 0.70% in Q1 FY 25

scores.rationale: Consistently grew credit well above system growth across the period — 9% YoY domestic vs banking system 3.28% in FY23, then 15.8% and 18.6% global advance growth in FY26/Q1FY27 — with RAM up ~19-20%, giving real share capture from a mid-sized base.
scores.quote: Global Gross Advances increased by 18.64% YoY from Rs. 6.72 lakh crore in Jun'25 to Rs. 7.98 lakh crore in Jun'26

scores.rationale: Genuine and long-standing international footprint being actively extended — 15+ countries, GIFT City FCSS participation, a live Kenya mobile banking app and a $1.2bn FCNR(B) plus $2bn OFCB/MTN mobilisation — though international NIM is structurally thin (0.98%-1.25%).
scores.quote: We have an international presence of more than 15 countries

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume-led with adverse pricing: global NIM fell from 3.07% (Q1FY25) to 2.52% (FY26/Q1FY27) even as the book grew ~16%, and management describes active undercutting on corporate pricing and concessions on home loans.
scores.quote: a lot of undercutting is happening within the banks also. Like banks are lending at 7.60% to 7.80% to these AAA advances

scores.rationale: The bank sits near the top, not the bottom, of the credit cycle — GNPA has fallen from 9.30% (Jun'22) to 1.81% (Jun'26), credit cost to 0.15% and PCR to 93.83%, leaving little further provisioning tailwind ahead of the FY28 ECL transition.
scores.quote: Gross NPA ratio improved by 111 bps YoY to 1.81% for Jun'26... Credit Cost declined to 0.15%

scores.rationale: End market is India's structurally expanding credit economy — repeated references to 7%+ GDP growth, Viksit Bharat 2047, and secular MSME/retail/agri credit demand that has supported 12-16% business growth every year.
scores.quote: the outlook for the Indian economy remains constructive, supported by stable consumption patterns, continued public investment and healthy credit demand

scores.rationale: Organic-only growth with strong capital and provisioning buffers — CRAR 18.69% vs 11.5% mandated, PCR 93.83% — funding raised prudently via infra bonds/SIDBI/NABARD rather than expensive bulk deposits, and no appetite for large M&A.
scores.quote: our CRAR is 18.01 % as against the RBI's mandated 11.5 %

scores.rationale: Execution has been persistent and consistent over four years (digital roadmap, deposit franchise projects UDAAN/ZDC, NPA reduction), but strategy is largely set by government and RBI agendas — ECLGS, PM-Surya Ghar, Viksit Bharat, LCR/DCCO/ECL circulars — so independence is limited.
scores.quote: the bank is focusing on inclusive and consistent growth to become the catalyst in the Government's vision for Viksit Bharat 2047

scores.rationale: Calls are workmanlike and data-driven, led by a career PSU banker with no personality-building; commentary sticks to ratios, guidance and operational initiatives.
scores.quote: My remarks today are divided into three parts. First being the institutional initiatives. The second being the business and the third being profitability and asset quality.

scores.rationale: Evidence is of structural staffing and role creation — 82 Resource Managers, Zonal Deposit Centres, a new GM-headed sales vertical, BOI Services 'feet on street' — but nothing on talent development or a leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: we are creating vertical for the sales vertical in the Bank for the 1st time where the General Manager will be in charge for sales and marketing

scores.rationale: Management volunteers uncomfortable facts and quantifies them — the deposit-advance funding gap, an above-ideal CD ratio attributed to a resource crunch, sector-level stress from the West Asia crisis, and a downward NIM guidance revision to 2.90%.
scores.quote: If you see our CD ratio it is around 82-83 %, which is high because obviously there is a crunch of resources

scores.rationale: The headline improvement — GNPA 9.30% to 1.81%, credit cost to 0.15%, profit up 36% — is largely a system-wide PSU credit-cycle recovery and lower provisioning, while the skill-dependent metrics (NIM 3.07% to 2.52%, CASA ratio 44.70% to 36.68%) have deteriorated.
scores.quote: Global NIM stood at 2.52% in FY26 against 2.82% in FY25

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position anywhere — the bank competes on price for both assets and liabilities and is losing deposit share to non-bank asset classes.
scores.quote: lot of funds are flowing out of the banking system into other asset class like equity, like mutual fund, like gold

scores.rationale: Weak switching costs — deposits are migrating out of the system, CASA ratio fell from 44.70% (Jun'22) to 36.68% (Jun'26), and even home-loan borrowers require rate concessions to be retained.
scores.quote: CASA ratio stood at 36.68%

scores.rationale: Indian banking is a fragmented, intensely competitive market where corporate borrowers hold pricing power and deposit customers are being bid for by every bank.
scores.quote: there has been a lot of competition among the Banks how to fund this credit growth which is coming

scores.rationale: Regulatory licensing barriers are high, but pricing behaviour is plainly irrational — explicit undercutting on AAA corporate loans at 20% RWA and bulk deposits bid up to ~7.5%.
scores.quote: a lot of undercutting is happening within the banks also

scores.rationale: The bank has grown credit faster than the system, implying share gain from weaker PSU peers, but no specific donator is identified and BOI itself concedes ground on pricing to private banks.
scores.quote: we have done a growth of about 9% year-on-year, vis-à-vis industry and banking system's growth of 3.28%

scores.rationale: A large listed nationalised bank with 5,500 branches, hybrid analyst meets with pan-India coverage and a PR firm handling investor queries — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: attended physically as well as virtually by our analyst from Pan India

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power in a commoditised product — margins compressed through the period and management concedes rate concessions are necessary to hold customers.
scores.quote: in home loans where some concession has to be necessarily given to keep pace with the market competition

scores.rationale: Sovereign-backed trust underpins a genuinely retail, sticky liability base — ~81-82% of domestic deposits are CASA or retail term with only ~13.6% bulk — and depositors accept below-market rates for that certainty.
scores.quote: nearly 86% of our deposit is either CASA or Retail term deposit, which is helping us to maintain our cost of deposit

scores.rationale: Strong and deliberately deepening accessibility — 5,500 branches plus 600 new ones over FY25-27, ~250 AD/NRI branches, video-KYC digital onboarding, UPI sound-boxes and a new field sales force.
scores.quote: Then we have our subsidiary which we call the BOI Service Ltd, where we have started Campaign "Feet on street"

scores.rationale: The mix is well matched on the retail/RAM side (58.30% of advances, 81-82% retail deposits) which suits a trust-based PSU proposition, but the 45% corporate book is won on price rather than switching-cost lock-in.
scores.quote: RAM advances increased by 19.75% YoY... constituting 58.30% of Advances in Jun'26

scores.rationale: Digital spend is catch-up rather than edge — the Rs.1,000 crore platform slipped past its Sept 2023 deadline, and the initiatives cited (UPI in app, virtual debit card, choose-your-account-number) are table stakes matched across the industry.
scores.quote: we want to see Bank of India to be only on the digital map as other banks are also running very fast on that trend

scores.rationale: No self-reinforcing network — payment rails used (UPI, Bharat Connect, M-PESA, TReDS) are industry utilities that confer no scale advantage on BOI.
scores.quote: The Bank has launched the Bharat Connect Biller Operating Services

scores.rationale: Reach is the bank's most defensible asset — 5,500 domestic branches across 69 zonal and 13 FGM offices, 3 RRBs, ~250 AD/NRI branches and operations in 15+ countries feeding a global FCNR mobilisation.
scores.quote: we are seeing this money coming from across the globe... whether it is USA or Canada, whether it is in the four countries in Africa

scores.rationale: Capex has been steady on store renovations, franchise/SIS expansion, ERP and moulds across all four years, but incremental returns are poor — revenue was flat-to-negative through FY24-FY26 and the company has been monetising land and closing plants rather than adding productive capacity.
scores.quote: over the last 4 years, revenue growth has remained largely stagnant despite multiple strategic initiatives

scores.rationale: A&P is a disciplined 250-300bps of sales with sustained brand-building (Hush Puppies first-ever campaign, Try and Fly, Ballerina) and is now showing measurable payback in brand consideration and two consecutive quarters of accelerating growth.
scores.quote: Brand consideration has shown a good trajectory, moved down to 66, which is the highest

scores.rationale: There is real product/technology investment (Power technology, central product design capability, comfort/style pivots) but management admits only a fraction has reached consumers, so long-term R&D efficiency is unproven.
scores.quote: There is a huge amount of investment that are going in. I think only 10% of that is what has come out into what is consumer facing

scores.rationale: Apart from a passing reference to 'inorganic' SIS additions, no acquisitions are discussed across the four years, leaving nothing to judge.
scores.quote: both organic as well as inorganic combination

scores.rationale: No discussion of buybacks, dividend policy or any distribution framework appears in the excerpts.

A deliberate shift to an asset-light structure — franchise-led expansion with working capital loaded on partners, land monetisation, plant closure and inventory down 28% over two years — but the moat protecting it is weak in a self-described fragmented market.
scores.quote: an ROCE by default franchise is much better because a lot of the inventory and working capital is loaded onto the franchise

scores.rationale: Rather than capturing share, Bata has ceded it — negative same-store sales, four stagnant years, mass price points under stress for 7-8 quarters, and new competition from Metro's brand acquisition and global digital-first brands.
scores.quote: It has been evidently negative, Saurabh, but lower single-digit negative

scores.rationale: Credible, consistently executed domestic penetration — franchise into tier 3-5 towns where Bata is the first organised retailer, MBO town coverage from ~1,100 to 1,670, and 2,000+ EBOs — though export/overseas expansion remains only an intent.
scores.quote: especially in the tier three to tier five, where we are obviously, in many, many towns, the first organized retailer

scores.rationale: Premium mix (Hush Puppies, Power, Floatz) consistently outpaces the base and full-price sales now grow ~2x total, but the recent recovery is explicitly volume-backed rather than price-led.
scores.quote: pleased to have a second consecutive quarter of accelerating growth, and it was volume backed

scores.rationale: The business appears to be emerging from a multi-quarter trough in mass consumption, with GST 2.0 rate cuts described as a structural tailwind and two consecutive quarters of accelerating growth after years of decline.
scores.quote: an underlying structural impact of GST 2.0, which should continue in general for the foreseeable future

scores.rationale: Indian footwear is a large, under-penetrated and formalising market — management points to awareness far exceeding availability and a GST-driven structural demand shift — even if Bata has not been capturing that growth.
scores.quote: The brand is extremely high on awareness... How do we make sure that our availability reaches up to that awareness

scores.rationale: Purely organic strategy with no large M&A, structural cost action (plant closure, VRS, Faridabad land monetisation), franchise-led capital-light expansion and conservative accounting of ERP costs.
scores.quote: we have been trying to improve the structural cost by closure of plant operations

scores.rationale: Gunjan Shah has stayed with the same multi-year agenda through a prolonged growth drought — Floatz over three years, ZBM scaled 400 to 550 stores toward full network, and a six-quarter inventory programme — showing tenacity if not yet results.
scores.quote: Floatz is a classic example that we have been on it for almost 3 years now

scores.rationale: Management commentary is operational and metric-driven with no personality cult; the CEO consistently discusses process metrics, store counts and inventory turns rather than promoting himself.
scores.quote: There are many other process metrics, which I'll not drain out here

scores.rationale: Little evidence of systematic talent development beyond variable pay at stores, while the CFO seat turned over three times (Vidhya Srinivasan to Anil Somani to Amit Aggarwal) and board composition churned heavily across FY22-FY26, suggesting a thin internal pipeline.
scores.quote: what I feel is right at par variable structure performance pay at stores at about 30% as per design

scores.rationale: Management openly labels its own results disappointing, discloses negative same-store sales, walks analysts line-by-line through four exceptional items, and concedes shortfalls — though it declines to share channel- and brand-level growth data.
scores.quote: a longer term trend line, obviously disappointing revenue growth last quarter

scores.rationale: The narrative quality (ZBM, product funnel, brand consideration) far outruns the financial outcome, so the strong storytelling should be discounted — turnaround has been promised since 2022 and delivered only 3-5% growth by FY26.
scores.quote: we are hopeful that that reversal journey will give us positive momentum in the balance of the year

scores.rationale: Bata owns a genuinely iconic position in the Indian consumer's mind, but that mindshare is ageing into 'legacy' among younger buyers and confers no monopoly-like economics.
scores.quote: people still consider Bata as a legacy brand and the younger consumer... prefer new and cool-looking brands apart from Bata

scores.rationale: Footwear retail carries no switching costs or captive aftermarket — consumers reselect every purchase, and management's answer to competition is product and accessibility, not lock-in.
scores.quote: there is a consumer trend, there is a competition, there are trends that we can identify

scores.rationale: Management explicitly describes the market at both the value and premium ends as highly fragmented rather than consolidated.
scores.quote: both ends, the market is significantly fragmented. So it's not like it's a duopoly or a monopoly

scores.rationale: Barriers are low and rivalry is intensifying — Metro acquiring competing brand rights, global digital brands taking younger consumers — while the industry runs seasonal EOSS discounting and Bata itself manages markdowns as a core metric.
scores.quote: there is another brand class where rights have been acquired by Metro. Plus we are seeing incremental focus of expansion in terms of their value brand

scores.rationale: A vast unorganised base in tier 3-5 towns offers share to take, but over the review period Bata has been the donator rather than the taker, with negative SSSG and mass-segment stress.
scores.quote: the mass price points continue to have some amount of stress

scores.rationale: Bata is a heavily covered large-cap consumer name with calls hosted by ICICI, YES, B&K and 360 ONE and questions from Goldman Sachs, Fidelity, JM and IIFL — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: The next question is from the line of Saurabh Kundan from Goldman Sachs

scores.rationale: High unaided awareness and record brand consideration coexist with weak pricing power — persistent markdowns, EOSS dependence and a brand image losing aspirational pull with young consumers.
scores.quote: My discounting on an average is at high single digit

scores.rationale: Customers buy Bata for dependable comfort and quality, evidenced by NPS of 70, a CII zero-defect award, falling customer returns and a sustained availability programme lifting fill rates 1,000bps.
scores.quote: Net promoter score... has shown significant improvement at 70 there is a gain of almost 700 basis points versus 2021

scores.rationale: Accessibility is Bata's strongest customer benefit — 2,000+ EBOs, ~20,000 MBOs across 1,670 towns, 700+ omnichannel fulfilling stores, quick-commerce tie-ups and kiosks, with direct field-force reach to 50,000 outlets.
scores.quote: we now have almost 700-plus stores that are fulfilling online orders

scores.rationale: The customer base is retail, where intangible brand pull is the right lever, yet Bata's brand equity is eroding with younger buyers; the corporate/industrial (I&D safety) leg with 2,000+ KRO reach is growing but still small.
scores.quote: Our I&D promise business continues to expand through the KRO network, reach is now 2,000 plus

scores.rationale: Technology is applied (ERP/MS Dynamics, ZBM, Bata app, Power product tech) but it is catch-up operational IT rather than a proprietary edge, and the ERP was a large expense charged off rather than a differentiator.
scores.quote: we have also charged off the complete expense on our IT projects, especially the largest one being ERP

scores.rationale: Footwear retail here is a straightforward product-and-store model with no two-sided dynamic; nothing in four years of calls indicates value rising with user count — the app is a D2C channel, not a network.
scores.quote: we also have launched our Bata app and now almost 14% of our D2C business comes through the app

scores.rationale: The physical and omnichannel reach — 2,000 EBOs, ~50,000 MBO outlets with direct field reach, 1,670 towns, franchise partners queuing to open more, and the largest omnichannel network — is the one asset rivals genuinely cannot replicate.
scores.quote: the kind of demand that we see from potential franchise partners is enormous, it is more a question of our bandwidth

scores.rationale: Capex is minimal and unquantified — nearly all operating cash is distributed rather than reinvested, with only passing mention of solar and backward integration.
scores.quote: we have paid out almost 90% of the cumulated operating cashflow over last 4 years

scores.rationale: Consistent, deliberate brand investment (brand building cited as a top-line driver, digital brand recognition, product authentication) sustained across all three calls.
scores.quote: We have doubled down on brand building

scores.rationale: A steady flow of new launches (Vayego, Council, Dekalb hybrids, Bicota, Etcio Star) now explicitly selected for bottom-line impact, though the R&D itself is parent-funded rather than local.
scores.quote: we really have new launches coming in that do both... they also bring a profitability profile with it that it has bottom line impact

scores.rationale: No acquisitions in the window at all — the activity is the other way (Environmental Science and Crystal seeds divestments) used to streamline the portfolio.
scores.quote: Some of it started with divestment... that was more driven from a global perspective

scores.rationale: A coherent, explicitly stated and defended distribution policy — ~77-80%+ payout sustained, and dividend held at Rs.90 even after EPS fell to 126 — but dividends only, no valuation-disciplined buybacks.
scores.quote: as a Board, therefore, the dividend policy remains, or the dividend distribution remains, intact

scores.rationale: Asset-light model delivering 33% ROCE that expanded 500bps over four years, protected by owned brands (Roundup, Dekalb, Nativo) and a proprietary germplasm position.
scores.quote: return of capital employed, we also saw good growth of 190 basis points compared to the last year ending with 33%

scores.rationale: Explicit share capture in under-penetrated corn geographies and a stated runway in core CP, though partially offset by deliberate retreat from low-margin territories.
scores.quote: we've gone into areas where, in the past we were very, very timid; Karnataka etc. where we're really, really taking market share

scores.rationale: Expansion is intra-India (new corn geographies, BLF centre rollout) rather than international, and is now selective — credible but modest in ambition.
scores.quote: We're seeing that a broad portfolio is allowing us to go into new geographies

scores.rationale: Pricing power visibly broke down in FY25 when Chinese supply blocked price pass-through, and growth has been carried by corn volume; mix-led margin repair is only just beginning.
scores.quote: the supply and the prices from China were such, that it limited our ability to pass any price increase in the market

scores.rationale: FY25 was described as the trough ('perfect storm') on input costs and margins, with input-price stabilisation and 100bps gross-margin expansion already visible — an identifiable upturn.
scores.quote: This year, we are seeing stabilization in our input prices... more than 100 basis point expansion in our Gross Margin

scores.rationale: Multiple genuine secular drivers — corn becoming the third field crop (doubled in five years, 15-16% CAGR), the structural shift from insecticides to herbicides on labour shortage, and nutrition demand for 1.7bn people.
scores.quote: India is still the only large agricultural market in the world where herbicides do not dominate the business... This is changing very, very quickly

scores.rationale: Sustained OpEx discipline below inflation, no leverage or big M&A, and vigilant channel/receivables management — but capital discipline manifests as payout rather than counter-cyclical investment.
scores.quote: CAGR of 9% while also very, very prudently managing OpEx. So, you see OpEx, CAGR is only 6.1% that's also well below inflation

scores.rationale: Genuine long-horizon behaviour — refusal to steer quarterly, refusal to stuff the channel, and the multi-year DSR bet scaled from 5,000 to over 1 lakh acres — though strategy is visibly set by the German parent.
scores.quote: We are not steering the business on the quarterly and we're ensuring that... we actually improve our business and don't fill the channel with material

scores.rationale: Communication is technical and agronomy-focused with no personality cult; the leaders present as operators, not celebrities, even while running a global brand.
scores.quote: I've spent more than 7 years in the Country now and more than 25 years in the Company

scores.rationale: Claims of industry-leading talent and an internally-promoted CFO (25 years in the group) sit against heavy churn in the MD/Chairman ranks across FY2021-FY2026 with no described succession system.
scores.quote: this is my 25th year with Bayer Group of Companies

scores.rationale: Repeatedly owns bad outcomes and its own shortcomings — the honest FY24, the receivables mistake, and even conceding that investor disclosure has not been good enough.
scores.quote: we did have some issues with receivables, and yes, we've learned our lesson

scores.rationale: Management itself separates results from skill by attributing swings to monsoon, Ukraine energy costs and Chinese pricing, which limits halo risk but also shows much of the outcome is not management-driven.
scores.quote: full year 2024-25, in some sense, was a perfect storm

scores.rationale: Owns near-monopoly mind-share positions in specific segments — Roundup in glyphosate, Dekalb in corn, and the acknowledged lead breeder position in Indian corn.
scores.quote: corn is the one for the Country which is really, really important, and we are the main breeders in the country, there's no question about it

scores.rationale: Some system lock-in via the corn-seed-to-herbicide pull-through and hybrid loyalty, but no regional monopoly or true captive aftermarket — farmers can and do switch.
scores.quote: the link between our corn seeds and Laudis, the corn herbicide remains very strong

scores.rationale: Management describes crop protection as a highly competitive market where Chinese supply sets prices and margins get squeezed — the opposite of a stable oligopoly with a powerless customer.
scores.quote: it is a very competitive market and you would have seen that in how some of margins play out, how prices have been playing out

scores.rationale: Pricing was irrational enough that a global leader could not pass on cost inflation, and off-patent generics from China dictated realisations despite regulatory barriers.
scores.quote: especially not if the overall agriculture is not picking up enough stuff from China

scores.rationale: No weak competitor pool is identified — the pressure runs the other way from Chinese suppliers — though industry-wide corn seed production shortages leave some supply gap to capture.
scores.quote: almost the industry trying to catch up with being able to produce enough corn seeds

scores.rationale: This is the listed arm of the world's largest agri-input company, top-5 country for the group, with global CEO visits and heavy investor/regulatory attention — the antithesis of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: we are in the top 5 countries in the world

scores.rationale: Real brand pull with farmers and authentication-driven preference for genuine product, but the FY25 inability to price shows the intangible does not fully convert into pricing power.
scores.quote: Brand recognition and protection are key to ensure farmers invest in what will lead to the right outcomes for them

scores.rationale: The core proposition is certainty — genuine product, agronomic advice and consistent hybrid performance in a market with a documented trust gap and counterfeit problem.
scores.quote: allows farmers to scan their products they bought to see whether it's genuine

scores.rationale: Deep last-mile intimacy through 1,500+ Better Life Farming centres, field officer territories and digital FarmRise reach, though the newest plan deliberately thins physical presence in low-margin areas.
scores.quote: With our more than 1500 Better Life Farming centres we and our partners cater to the farming community's needs

scores.rationale: Benefit type is well matched to a retail smallholder base — brand, trust, agronomic advice and financing access to ~20 million smallholders — rather than a corporate TCO pitch.
scores.quote: we reach almost 20 million out of the 50 million smallholders that we as Bayer CropScience touch globally

scores.rationale: Access to the parent's multi-product pipeline and breeding technology gives a real edge (DSR-bred rice, new hybrids, Bicota), but key technologies such as HT are not available to it in India.
scores.quote: we don't have the HT, for example, but we're going to be seeing the next systemic change to agriculture

scores.rationale: The digital platform and BLF/FPO partner ecosystem create some reinforcing effects and data feedback, but nothing self-reinforcing or two-sided in a defensible sense.
scores.quote: we see the uptake coming on our own platforms exponentially

scores.rationale: Claimed best-in-industry channel discipline plus a partner retail network competitors would struggle to replicate, tempered by the deliberate handover of some territories to partners.
scores.quote: We lead the industry in channel discipline, I am convinced of that
